An extraordinarily rare blue diamond ring is expected to fetch as much as £2 million when it goes up for sale next month.

Auctioneers Elmwood’s stated that the jewel will be only the third blue diamond weighing over eight carats ever offered at auction in the UK.

Featuring an 8.03 carat Fancy Light Blue diamond, the piece is set to appear in Elmwood’s Fine Jewellery sale in London on 1 October.

Elmwood’s said the only other blue diamonds weighing more than eight carats ever auctioned in the UK are the 70.21 carat "Idol’s Eye", sold at Christie’s in London in 1865, and the Wittelsbach Diamond, sold at Sotheby’s in London in 2008.

The pear-shaped diamond ring is being sold by a collector in Glasgow and carries an estimate of £1.5 million to £2 million.

open image in gallery The ring, featuring a pear-shaped blue diamond, is being sold by a collector in Glasgow and is estimated to fetch £1.5 million to £2 million ( PA )

Joe Kendrick, head of sale at Elmwood’s auctioneers, said: “An 8.03 carat natural blue diamond is an extraordinary rarity in its own right, but what adds to its allure is its place in British auction history.

“To offer only the third blue diamond above eight carats ever seen at auction in the UK and the largest pear-shaped example, is a remarkable moment for Elmwood’s and for collectors of exceptional coloured diamonds.

“Coming from a Scottish collector, the ring is a truly once in a lifetime piece.

“Its combination of size, colour, clarity and elegant pear shape also gives this stone an exceptionally compelling presence and we therefore expect wide interest.”

open image in gallery Auctioneers Elmwood’s said the jewel will be only the third blue diamond weighing more than eight carats ever offered at auction in the UK ( PA )

The blue diamond is set at the centre of the ring, which also has concentric borders of round brilliant cut pink and white diamonds.

Natural blue diamonds are described as being among the rarest of all coloured diamonds.

Their colour is linked to trace amounts of boron incorporated into the gem’s crystal structure.

In the past, blue diamonds were mainly sourced from India and Brazil, however in more recent times they have also been found in South Africa’s Cullinan Mine.

News.title: England learn more in scrappy Sri Lanka win than in summer of white-ball walkovers
News.content:
You do not expect spinners to dominate at Chester-le-Street, but this hot summer has produced strange events, none more so than Jacks recording the second-best figures by an England spinner in one-day international cricket having previously only taken three wickets in 16 games at home.

Sachindu Colombage, Sri Lanka’s debutant leggie who was playing club cricket in East Anglia a year ago, laid down a marker as he impressed with three for 44 starting with the wicket of Root, his first dismissal in one-day international cricket since February.

England’s 89-run win was completed by Jacks taking three for none in four balls as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 176, their run chase a timid effort when they had a sniff of victory after restricting England to 265 and preventing them from hitting a six for the first time in an innings since 2019.

Vice-captain Jacks has evolved under Harry Brook’s leadership from an opening batsman to middle-order finisher who can chip in with the ball. “He is just a good leader with bat ball and in the field. He is buying into everything we want to do,” Brook said. “We are always talking about adapting to conditions and he has done it really well since coming back in. He could have moaned and groaned about batting in the middle order and playing as an all-rounder but has accepted that will be his place for a long time.”

Brook thought England made “just about par” on a very dry pitch and was reluctant to shower too much praise on batting consultant Kevin Pietersen, whose spin class the day before concentrated on making runs on a slow surface. “It will take time, more than one day. He’s not a miracle worker but it helps the more opportunity we get,” Brook said.

England were stretched and Pietersen will be happy. He told them to think about their approach, that in this type of game “rotation of strike is incredibly important”. He was right, they ran well, apart from Rehan Ahmed, and did not hit a six in an innings for the first time in seven years.

When England batsmen tried to force the pace they perished. Ben Duckett, Root and Brook all had opportunities to build an innings without seeing it through and it required Jacks to tip the total to more than 250. He batted within himself at first, but hit four fours in a row in the 47th over in a late burst that took England to a winning score.

News.title: Africa faces new threat as chronic disease rate leaps
News.content:
Chronic ailments like heart disease, cancers and diabetes now account for almost half of deaths in Africa and will soon overtake the continent’s infectious disease toll, new research has found.

Between 1990 and 2023 the proportion of deaths caused by non-communicable diseases (NCDs) almost doubled, from 25 per cent to 45 per cent, with heart disease and strokes now the leading killers.

The shift is not unexpected: public health experts have long warned that although African countries are making huge strides cutting infectious disease deaths through vaccinations, better sanitation and improved healthcare, lifestyle changes pose a new threat.

But the continent is not necessarily ready to tackle this “epidemiological transition”, researchers warned, in a study published in the Lancet Global Health journal on Tuesday.

“Although the epidemiological transition is well recognised, the speed and scale of NCD growth in Africa is particularly concerning,” they wrote.

“Health systems face increasing demands for chronic disease management, yet low-resource settings remain poorly equipped, underfunded, and unable to provide adequate preventive or treatment services.”

News.title: Zika mosquitoes still breeding in London
News.content:
Dr Medlock said there is still “no conclusive” evidence about how the insects arrived, but it’s possible that someone brought them back from holiday in their luggage, or that mosquito eggs were hidden on a tropical plant.

The mosquitoes are very temperature sensitive – they typically survive and multiply between 25C and 30C – and the UK has historically been too cold. But the species are gradually making their way north through Europe, after successive summers of record heat.

As temperatures drop in the coming weeks, the UKHSA hopes London’s invasive mosquitoes will die off naturally – though an unprecedented El Niño has made the predicament more challenging.

“This is a tropical mosquito, so the model has convinced me this won’t survive the winter,” Dr Medlock said. “Although we’ve got El Niño, [so] it’s very mild – it’s certainly warm enough still in East London [for the insects to survive].”

Diseases such as dengue and Zika virus do not typically circulate in Britain, but an infected traveller returning from a country where the diseases are present could carry the virus back with them.

If an invasive mosquito then bit an infected person, it could potentially catch and spread on the disease to others.

Several countries in Europe, including France, Italy and Spain, have started to see local transmission of mosquito-borne viruses, including dengue fever and West Nile virus, in recent years as the climate becomes more suitable for mosquitoes to survive and multiply.

Just last week, a third person died in Frankfurt, Germany, from malaria despite having no travel history, after mosquitoes infected with the disease were imported into the country on an aeroplane and subsequently infected eight people over the summer.

“We [already] see imported cases of malaria, dengue and chikungunya each year, with significant associated mortality and morbidity,” Dr Phillip Veal, a consultant in public health at the UKHSA, said.

“But if we [in Britain] follow the pattern of Europe, and all models suggest we will, Aedes albopictus and other Aedes species may become established. We’ve got a window of opportunity to do something, to prepare, to be ready, to fulfil our mission of protecting the public,” Dr Veal said.

News.title: Tax rises ‘virtually inevitable’ after £8bn borrowing blow
News.content:
Tax rises are “virtually inevitable” after official figures showed the Treasury has borrowed £8bn more than expected so far this year.

Economists said the Chancellor faced an “uncomfortable” Budget after the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said spending outstripped tax receipts by £18.3bn in August, £3.5bn more than expected.

It means John Healey, the Chancellor, has borrowed £77.3bn so far this financial year, which is £8.1bn more than forecast.

Reacting to the figures, Emma Reynolds, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, warned of “tough decisions” in Mr Healey’s Budget.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “The jump in borrowing in August compared to last year sets the stage for what is likely to be a much trickier Budget than Andy Burnham or Healey anticipated when they came to power.

“Another round of tax rises in October now looks inevitable.”

Philip Shaw, an economist at Investec, added: “We suspect that some tax increases are virtually inevitable.”

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the Chancellor would need to raise up to £14bn to restore the £24bn of fiscal headroom left by his predecessor Rachel Reeves to balance the books.

The Government’s debt interest bill soared to £8.8bn last month, according to the ONS, the biggest August figure since records began in 1997.

So far this year, the Treasury has spent £50bn on debt interest – £2bn more than forecast in March.

Nick Ridpath, an economist at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said: “Debt interest spending is a worryingly large share of overall government spending.

“Both higher borrowing costs and higher inflation make life harder for a Chancellor who is looking to bring down borrowing and to spend more on government priorities.”

Higher prices caused by the Iran war mean the Chancellor must pay more interest on the country’s huge stock of inflation-linked debt.

Inflation is also pushing up the welfare bill. The Government spent almost £30bn in August on benefits, 7pc more than a year ago.

Despite this, the Treasury continued to see substantial tax receipts. Income tax, capital gains, and National Insurance receipts stood at £231bn in the financial year to August.

That is £16.6bn higher than the same period a year ago.

Inheritance tax receipts also grew. They have risen to £3.8bn so far this financial year, a £100m increase compared with a year ago.

Ms Reynolds, the Treasury minister, said: “At a time when debt interest costs billions of pounds that could otherwise be spent on improving lives, we must always know where the money is coming from to pay for public services.

“That is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty.”

The figures also showed total debt rose to £2.985tn in August, taking the level just shy of £3tn.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said: “Labour has lost control of the public finances.

“It takes a rare fiscal incontinence to have both the highest tax take in history and see borrowing still shoot up.”

News.title: France releases infertile Asian tiger mosquitoes to fight dengue threat
News.content:
French cities are fighting the growing threat of diseases like dengue, chikungunya and Zika in mainland Europe by releasing millions of sterile male Asian tiger mosquitoes.

Terratis, a new company in the southern city of Montpellier, is breeding infertile males on an industrial scale as a long-term solution to the rapid spread of the disease-carrying insects.

The sterile males are bred at a factory in the southern city of Montpellier and then released in urban hot zones where the mosquitoes are most prevalent. After they have mated, females reproduce only empty eggs for the remainder of their lives.

“By using this technique, the mosquitoes will have no descendants and then, in theory, we can reduce the population with each generation,” said Clelia Oliva, the founder of Terratis.

“We are confident of being able to achieve a reduction of between 70 and 90 per cent in the towns in which we are releasing the sterile mosquitoes.”

The company, which started only two years ago, has experienced a dramatic surge in demand in the last few years as France tries to deal with the invasive species.

News.title: ‘42 surgeries in 48 hours’: Doctors face extreme pressure in South Sudan
News.content:
Dr Mathiang Agany had no idea what was coming.

On a humid morning in April, scores of patients were rushed into his basic hospital in rural South Sudan after a shoot out between rival gangs. As the most senior doctor, Dr Agany, a maternal health specialist, had to perform 42 surgeries in just 48 hours.

Working alongside a second surgeon, a nurse and an anaesthetist, Dr Agany, 44, carefully extracted bullets from the vital organs of nine patients.

In 22 cases, he glued together fractured bones; and in four others he clamped damaged tissues shut and repaired torn organs.

Over the same 48 hour period, he also delivered seven babies through emergency c-sections.

“You are tired... but you can relax later,” he told The Telegraph over a video call.

“My job [was] to keep people alive”.

Separate to the ruinous four-year civil war in neighbouring Sudan, the violence plaguing South Sudan is inter-communal, a self-perpetuating cycle of cattle raiding, territorial disputes and revenge attacks carried out by armed youth militias from pastoral communities known as Titweng (“cattle guard”).

Young children were among the victims, including a four-year-old boy, whose leg was fractured by a gunshot, and a nine-month-old baby girl whose chest was grazed by the same bullet that killed her father.

News.title: Afghan medical students face expulsion from Pakistan
News.content:
An educational lifeline for young Afghan women banned by the Taliban from training as doctors in their homeland is in jeopardy after Pakistan’s medical authorities tried to have them expelled.

Several hundred Afghan female students studying across the border in Pakistan have been threatened with removal, amid rising tensions and tit-for-tat exchanges between the neighbours.

The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) which regulates medical education earlier this month ordered medical and dental colleges with Afghan students to kick them out.

Within days, major institutions including King Edward Medical University (KEMU), Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College, and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences, had ordered Afghan students to leave.

The nationwide order was estimated to have affected around 1,000 Afghan students, with 35 per cent of those thought to be female students.

Provincial high courts have now temporarily halted the expulsion pending further hearings, but Afghan students told The Telegraph they were terrified their careers would be ended.

“The government’s decision aimed to send us to the Stone Age because the Taliban in Afghanistan have banned female education,” said Sabiha Daftani, one of the 22 Afghan students given orders on September 7 by KEMU in Lahore on to leave within 24 hours.

“The fear is constant and haunting us,” she said.

Sports.title: Saints icon Charlie Austin begs FA not to ruin Southampton boss Tonda Eckert’s career with six-month spygate ban
Sports.content:
Next

CHARLIE AUSTIN has pleaded with FA chiefs to leave Tonda Eckert alone and let him get on with his managerial career.

The Southampton boss faces a crucial FA meeting on Thursday after his club were caught sending a spy to Middlesbrough ahead of their play-off semi-final.



And the Championship team also admitted to snooping on Reading and Oxford.

The German coach could be slapped with a SIX-MONTH ban on top of the club having already been docked four points this season and chucked out of last May’s £200million play-off final against Hull.



Former Saints striker Austin said: “I think we should just move on.

“The punishment has been done. They got taken out of this game, which is worth millions.

“Eckert is a young coach. He made a mistake, he’s admitted he’s made a mistake, and he’s learned from it.

“Just let him get on with his career now. It’s ridiculous this has been dragged out further.”

Austin played 71 games for the Saints and keeps in close touch with what is happening down on the South Coast.

And the former Premier League hitman insists the whole saga is now overshadowing Saints’ impressive efforts on the pitch.



Eckert has received death threats and is constantly ridiculed at away stadiums as the FA disciplinary procedure plays out



Austin explained: “It’s gone on too much now. What happened last season happened and they want the dark cloud to disappear.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“We’re talking about minus four points they were docked but because they’ve started the season brilliantly that has become an irrelevance.

“The FA need to put this to bed — and let Eckert and Southampton get on with their lives.”



SunSport understands from sources at the club that there is a real concern that the FA might go for the nuclear six-month ban.

Eckert claims he was not aware that the practice of analysing opponents’ training sessions was prohibited in England as it is widespread where he has previously coached in Europe.

And it is a fact the EFL is the only football competition in world football where there is a rule banning the practice.

The FA themselves do not have a specific rule written down banning it either — but because Eckert has broken a competition’s rule they believe he has brought the game into disrepute.

Southampton owner Dragan Solak has vowed to stand by Eckert but the German’s position will be untenable if he is out for six months.



A source said: “Dragan was furious the spygate scandal ever happened but believes any lengthy ban for Eckert would be out of line. He wants him to stay but of course a six-month ban changes the dial.”

Austin, 37, has retired from football after a career that saw him climb from the Wessex League to the Premier League — playing notably for Swindon, Burnley, QPR, Southampton and West Brom.

And speaking at a sponsorship launch for the EFL Trophy — now to be known as the Jersey Mike’s Trophy — Austin insists his career only reached the heights it did because he cut his teeth in non-league for the likes of Hungerfood and Poole playing men’s football.

The Jersey Mike’s Trophy allows managers of Premier League and Championship academies to blood their kids against League One and Two teams.

And the lower tier sides also do likewise with some of their youth with a Wembley final at stake.

Sports.title: How Sir Alex Ferguson inadvertently set Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta on path to becoming Premier League ‘don’
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA is the “don” of the Premier League — and he looks here to stay.

The Arsenal boss has agreed terms on a new contract that will take his time in North London to ten years.



And it puts the Spaniard, 44, among a select group of Premier League managerial ‘Godfathers’ who have won the title and enjoyed long careers at their clubs.

Arsene Wenger was in charge of the Gunners for 22 years, while Sir Alex Ferguson did five more than that at Manchester United.



Pep Guardiola also managed a decade at Manchester City before he called it quits in the summer and Jurgen Klopp hit nine years with Liverpool.

Arteta is now set to follow in their footsteps and pundit Jamie Carragher argued this month how the Gunners boss now rules the roost in the Prem.



The former Liverpool defender, 48, explained: “He is the don at the moment. He is the Premier League champion.”

The power that Arteta wields at Arsenal — and within the English top flight — makes staying put an attractive option.

Carragher’s comments came after the Spaniard had a pop at the refereeing in the Gunners’ win at Sunderland this month.

Even though his side had won 2-0, Arteta made sure the decision to award the Black Cats a controversial penalty dominated the headlines.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In Carragher’s eyes, it was Arteta “becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League right now” — and using the clout he carries after leading the Gunners to title glory.

Carragher added: “One of the journalists made a point about, no matter what question you asked him, he kept going back to the penalty.

“So he was determined to get the narrative out that this won’t happen again to his club. We’ve seen it with Sir Alex Ferguson — we’ve seen it with Jose Mourinho.”

In a strange way, it was actually Sir Alex that set Arteta on the path to becoming a Premier League don.

Arsenal swooped for the Spaniard from Everton on deadline day in the summer of 2011, days after they lost 8-2 to United.



Arteta was one of four signings made by the Gunners during a mad trolley dash and over the next five years he got to learn under Frenchman Wenger.

That was followed by three educational seasons as Guardiola’s assistant at City before he took the Emirates reins in December 2019.

Battles with Klopp naturally followed, with the pair famously squaring up to each either on the touchline at Anfield.

Arteta was viewed then as the plucky Prem newcomer looking to fight the elite.



Now having joined that class, he is hungry for more and this new contract is proof of that.

So is the way that Arsenal have strengthened their squad this summer. The signings were all very much of a ‘win-now’ nature.

None of this ‘bread today, jam tomorrow’ spin from Wenger’s days.

The champions’ two biggest arrivals this summer were Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa for a combined cost of £125million.

Both are 28 and proven in the Premier League. Clearly, Arteta has no desire to hang around and wants to strike while the iron is hot.



By signing a new contract, he will send that message to others — both inside and outside the club.

Arsenal want to tie down the likes of David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber to fresh terms. That will be far easier now they know Arteta is staying.

The same goes for when the club pitches to potential new signings.

Arsenal still want a marquee forward and now whoever they target knows the manager is committed.



The question that remains, though, is how long for?

It is hard to see anyone replicating Sir Alex and Wenger’s stints in the modern era given the crazy schedule.

Guardiola and Klopp’s spells seem far more achievable and could work for Arteta.

Barcelona’s revamp of the Nou Camp will be done by then and manager Hansi Flick could have moved on, too.

A return to where Arteta began his career as a boy at Barca has always felt inevitable, or perhaps to Paris Saint-Germain.



It was at the French champions where the midfielder made his professional debut as an 18-year-old and he loved his time there.

But the concern for the fiercely ambitious Arteta must be that he will not find a club where he has the same power as Arsenal.

Guardiola discovered that and it is why he spent ten years at City — but only four at Barca.

Everything at the Emirates moves to Arteta’s beat and giving that up would not be easy.

After less than a year in charge, the Spaniard’s job title was changed from head coach to manager and he has never looked back.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Gunners have essentially been sculpted in his image — and he may not get the chance to do that again.

Arteta has also just joined the managerial royalty of the Premier League and does not look ready to give up that crown any time soon.

Sports.title: Joao Pedro issues statement on LinkedIn about Chelsea future a month after signing new contract

JOAO PEDRO has given a bizarre update on his playing future on LINKEDIN.

The Brazilian joined Chelsea from Brighton last summer in a £60million transfer.



Pedro, 24, penned a bumper new deal with the West Londoners in August which will keep him at Stamford Bridge until the summer of 2034.

And just a matter of weeks after tying his long-term future to the Blues, the striker has publicly reaffirmed his commitment to the club.



He wrote on his LinkedIn page: “Joining Chelsea Football Club was a huge moment for me, and looking back at everything that has happened since, I’m proud of how far we’ve come.

“I knew I was joining one of the biggest clubs in the world, with huge ambition and a special history.



“What I didn’t know was how quickly the club, the people here and life in London would become such an important part of my life.

“Since then, I’ve experienced some incredible moments in a Chelsea shirt.

“Winning the FIFA Club World Cup, having a season I’m proud of, being voted Player of the Season by our supporters and having the pride of becoming Chelsea’s number 9 are memories I’ll always carry with me.

“But this isn’t just about what we’ve already achieved.”

“For me, making a decision like this comes down to more than what is happening in the moment.

“It’s about looking at where you are, what you still want to achieve and whether the environment around you is helping you get there.

“I think there is a lot to consider when deciding whether to stay or take on something new.



“Progress doesn’t always mean choosing something different. Sometimes it’s recognising when you’re surrounded by the right people, still learning, still being challenged and still excited by what you’re building together.

“I believe in where this club is going, I believe in the people around me and I want to be part of what comes next.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney says everyone close to JJ Gabriel knew exit was coming and opens up on what Man Utd prodigy is really like
Sports.content:
Next

WAYNE ROONEY insists everyone close to JJ Gabriel always “KNEW” he’d eventually want to leave Manchester United.

The 15-year-old whizzkid rocked Red Devils chiefs earlier this month by formally asking them to cancel his registration.



Gabriel’s agent has already put the teenager in the shop window, lining up talks with European giants Bayern Munich and Real Madrid.

The attacking midfielder’s imminent departure, which could end up costing United MILLIONS, has come as a shock to the Old Trafford brass, although Rooney – whose son Kai has come through the ranks with Gabriel – insists it’s always been on the cards.



Speaking on Disney+’s Stick to United, he said: “I’ve seen JJ grow up because he’s been in Kai’s team throughout the years, and I think that anyone close to it knew that was coming.

“In fairness to Manchester United, they’ve done everything, they’ve done absolutely everything to keep him, to keep him at the club.



“I think it’s been known that there’s been a desire to go and play probably in Spain, I think, I might be wrong, but this is what you’ve heard over the years.

“The club have treated him probably differently to the other players because he is such a special talent.

“I know, I recognise, I understand that because I was that player at Everton and I was getting that treatment at Everton which was you’re getting a bit more, your parents get given stuff, you’re getting that special treatment more than the other players are getting.

“Which, as a club, you need to do to try and keep your better players.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“It’s just disappointing, of course, because he is such a top player and he’s a lovely kid.

“So you never know whether it’s gone too far and whether there is a chance to stay.

“But I think everyone close to it has probably known that that was going to come.”

Having watched Gabriel up close on a number of occasions, Rooney firmly believes United will be missing out on a future top talent.



The club’s all-time leading goalscorer said of the youngster: “He is a top player.

“His ability, his balance, he has shown he can go up the ages and score goals.

“The next step is first-team football where it’s different, and you never know until you’re in there.

“But he’s such a special talent who understands the game really well.

“At some point this season he would [have] made his debut for the first-team, I’d imagine, so that’s where it’s disappointing.”



United boss Michael Carrick insists the club will handle Gabriel’s seemingly imminent departure with the utmost care.

“It’s more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really.

“He’s certainly a young man. The situation is what it is.

“But we have to be a little bit careful about the exposure and how we jump on that.”

Sports.title: Former Chelsea ace ‘slapped in shocking restaurant bust-up’ after row with agent over commission on £13m transfer
Sports.content:

MALANG SARR was reportedly ambushed and slapped after one of his representatives missed out on a massive payday following his switch to Saudi Arabia.

The former Chelsea centre-back was dining with two of his new NEOM team-mates in Malaga, Spain, in July.



L’equipe reported that “a group of imposing Frenchmen” interrupted the private dining room – reserved for the club – and dragged the star aside where a very loud conversation followed.

They ordered Sarr not to move, whilst the rest of the gathering also froze.



The star was said to be dragged away and repeatedly slapped in the assault – claims Sarr has refuted to French media.

The heated argument was said to revolve around his move to Saudi where the 27-year-old is set to earn £13million over the next three years.



Sarr’s deal expired on June 30 and he was permitted to join a new club on a free – despite his market value estimated to be around £17.2m.

And the player agreed to a new contract in just two days – without any agent involvement.

The day after signing, Sarr was pictured next to a NEOM-appointed agent holding a club shirt.

But with several agents being in-and-around the ace over the last few months, one in particular was said to be deeply cut by the quick deal – worsened by the fact he had had dealings with NEOM in the past.

ANDROS TOWNSEND has revealed the unusual meals that he prepared to help recover from his freak accident with a pitch roller.

The former Tottenham and England winger, who now plays for PT Prachuap in Thailand, was run over by the machine while warming up at half-time.



Townsend, 35, thankfully came through the terrifying incident without serious injury, and was even able to come on as a substitute during the second half,.

But after the match, Townsend found his knee swelling and felt the need to aid his recovery with some specially prepared meals.



In an Instagram video the 13-cap star, who is no stranger to a quirky meal, said: “Over the next 24 hours, this is everything I ate to give my body what it needs to recover, support the inflammation process, and get me moving again without having to reach for medication.

“First up, six whole eggs. High-quality protein to support muscle repair.



“Then I started loading up on polyphenol-rich foods: blueberries, extra virgin olive oil, and raw cacao, which is packed with flavanols. These plant compounds have antioxidant and inflammation-reducing properties.

“Next, smoked salmon, packed with omega-3s, which are involved in inflammatory signalling and supporting muscle recovery.



“Raw cheese gives me calcium to support bone health. And then an orange gives me vitamin C, essential for making collagen.”

Far from being done, Townsend then revealed his painstakingly prepared second meal.

“And I paired that with kiwi for another big hit of vitamin C”.

Townsend finished his video by vowing: “Food is medicine.”

The shocking roller incident immediately went viral, with Townsend subsequently appearing on Piers Morgan Uncensored to explain what actually happened.

He said: “I didn’t see it coming. It was at half-time, we were going out to warm up. I saw two rollers on either side of the pitch.

“I remember thinking to myself, ‘I’ve never seen that before in my career, what are they doing?’



“But we got called to warm up. Didn’t think anything of it. The next I saw him was when I was literally underneath him and thankfully no serious damage.

“A couple of bumps and bruises but managed to walk away unscathed, luckily. Every time I see it, I’m cringing, I’m in disbelief. When I sent it to my kids, my kids thought it was AI.

“Literally, I had to explain to them, for the next ten minutes, that it was real. It’s horrible to watch back and to see what could have been.

“Thankfully, I was fortunate I did manage to fall on to the floor at the right time, so nothing snapped as the roller went over me. And I’m here today to laugh about and tell the story.”

Sports.title: Max Dowman handed England reality check as Arsenal star eyes long-standing record
Sports.content:
Max Dowman handed England reality check as Arsenal star eyes long-standing record

Max Dowman is tipped for huge things but, despite talk of an England call-up, the Arsenal teenager has been reminded that players have to progress through the age grades first

View 2 Images Max Dowman is making his way through the England age grades

Arsenal sensation Max Dowman has been told that he won't necessarily go straight into the England squad with the U21s seen as his next step.

‌



The 16-year-old, who became the Premier League's youngest ever goalscorer last season, has enjoyed a rapid rise and is now being talked up for a senior spot with the Three Lions. He has been Thomas Tuchel‘s radar since before the World Cup, but is poised to play with the U19s on Friday.

‌



Lee Carsley, the U21s boss, could see a host of his players step up after five players, including Declan Rice and Cole Palmer, pulled out of the England squad that have four matches in the next 10 days, starting with Spain on Saturday.

‌



But Carsley has made it clear that Dowman's next step will almost certainly be with the U21s, not the senior squad, as the coaches attempt to ensure he enjoys a natural progression, which they believe will lead to a long lasting England career.

He said: “It’s important players develop at their own pace. Max is an outstanding talent, the timing and the balance of when he comes to the Under-21s is inevitable.

Sports.title: Who really owns your club? Every Premier League team's ownership structure explained
Sports.content:
Premier League ownership is awash with private equity firms, multi-club groups and sovereign wealth funds. So, do you know who really controls your football club?

With the English top flight now the financial envy of all of European football, owning one of the 20 teams that call the league home can require serious financial backing.

Those who part with hundreds of millions are often unknown names to the general public. That is, unless they assume an executive role. Take Todd Boehly. Chelsea fans are now all too familiar with the American billionaire, who led the consortium that purchased the club from Roman Abramovich in 2022.

He stepped down as chairman last week after agreeing to sell his stake to co-owners Clearlake Capital. But what is this company and who are the people who make the calls? Mirror Football takes a look at the owners who actually run the show in the Premier League.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

7 outrageous Sir Jim Ratcliffe statements after Gary Lineker's attack on Man Utd owner READ MORE :

Premier League make feelings clear on VAR after 'significant' error in statement to clubs READ MORE :

Arsenal

Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE) holds a 100 per cent stake in Arsenal. They are an American sports and entertainment empire founded by billionaire Stan Kroenke. He is worth an estimated £21billion.

View 22 Images The Kroenkes witnessed their club lift the Premier League last season (Image: Getty)

KSE initially bought a minority stake in the Gunners in 2007 from ITV for £65million before launching a full buyout in 2018, when Kroenke purchased Russian oligarch Alisher Usmanov's 30 per cent stake for £550m.

‌



Whilst Stan is the ultimate financial authority, day-to-day oversight is handled by his son, Josh, who acts as the club's co-chair alongside his father.

Aston Villa

V Sports purchased a 55 per cent stake in Aston Villa in July 2018 for £30m, but just over a year later, they assumed 100 per cent control, saving the club from bankruptcy by settling debts. Egyptian billionaire Nassef Sawiris and American private equity investor Wes Edens jointly control the holding company.

Initially, Villa was purchased by NSWE, a company name both Sawiris and Edens created using their initials. But it rebranded to V Sports in 2021. Edens is the co-founder of Fortress Investment Group and Sawiris amassed his fortune through construction and chemicals.

View 22 Images Sawiris is Villa's executive chairman (Image: Getty)

‌



Whilst both act as co-chairmen, Sawiris assumes day-to-day control and is the main driving force behind high-level decisions. They also own stakes in Portuguese side Vitoria Guimaraes and French team FC Annecy. US investment firm Atairos bought into V Sports in late 2023 and is a 31 per cent shareholder.

Bournemouth

The Cherries are owned by Black Knight Football Club, a syndicate that acquired a 100 per cent stake in the club in December 2022 after previous owner Maxim Demin sold up for approximately £120m.

Bill Foley led the syndicate, which also features minority partners, including actor Michael B. Jordan and Cannae Holdings. Foley operates as the club's chairman. BKFC also maintains full ownership of French club FC Lorient - from which Bournemouth have signed players such as Dango Ouattara, now of Brentford, and Eli Junior Kroupi.

View 22 Images Foley calls the shots at the Vitality Stadium (Image: Getty)

‌



They also hold an interest in Moreirense FC of Portugal, Auckland FC of New Zealand and Hibernian of Scotland. Not to mention, as their name would suggest, they are the owners of the Vegas Golden Knights, a successful NHL ice hockey franchise.

Brentford

Lifelong Bees fan and British businessman Matthew Benham holds over 90 per cent of Brentford's equity. He began investing in the club in 2007, paying £3m initially to take over the club's loans, and took full ownership in 2012, operating through holding company Best Intentions Analytics Limited (BIA).

The other 10 per cent comprises other investors and a consortium through BIA. Benham remains the majority shareholder, though, and possesses total voting authority.

View 22 Images Benham first invested in Brentford nearly two decades ago (Image: Getty)

‌



British film director Matthew Vaughn, South African philanthropist Gary Lubner and Universal Music Group CEO Sir Lucian Grainge are among the stakeholders. Bees United, Brentford's supporters' trust, sold their equity stake in the club to Benham in 2012 but retains a Special Share, which guarantees fan representation on the board and grants veto power over major changes.

Brighton

Tony Bloom has revolutionised Brighton & Hove Albion since taking over as primary owner and chairman in 2009. The British entrepreneur, who made his fortune primarily through sports gambling, has invested hundreds of millions into the club's infrastructure, overseeing their move to the Amex Stadium in 2011.

Bloom holds an approximate 96 per cent stake in the club and as the majority shareholder, retains complete strategic control. He is aided by CEO Paul Barber, who helps with analytical models. Bloom also holds shares in Belgian team Royale Union Saint-Gilloise and Hearts.

View 22 Images Bloom has turned Brighton into a top-flight force (Image: Getty)

‌



The other roughly seven per cent of Brighton and Hove Albion Holdings Limited (the club's parent company) is divided among the likes of Barber, former club president Dick Knight and other local investors and shareholders. Historically, the club raised capital through fan-led campaigns.

Chelsea

As mentioned, Boehly has left Chelsea after selling his entire ownership stake to Clearlake Capital. He served as the club's chairman from May 2022 to earlier this month, partnering with US private equity firm Clearlake to buy the Blues from Abramovich via the consortium and parent company BlueCo for £2.5bn.

Investors Mark Walter and Hansjorg Wyss were also part of the takeover, but Clearlake always held the majority stake at 61.5 per cent. Now, both Boehly and business partner Walter have left and sold up to Clearlake Capital for £950m.

Behdad Eghbali and Jose Feliciano lead Clearlake and are now the near-exclusive controlling owners of BlueCo, which oversees other sporting assets, including the French club RC Strasbourg.

‌



View 22 Images Eghbali and Feliciano are the head honchos (Image: Getty)

The west Londoners no immediate plans to appoint a new chairperson, with Clearlake leading the way as 87.1 per cent owners. Wyss retains 12.9 per cent. Eghbali and Feliciano are billionaire financiers who co-founded Clearlake, which manages over £138bn in assets.

Coventry City

Sky Blues fans are more than familiar with their owner, Doug King, the British businessman who completed a total takeover of Coventry City in 2023.

King holds a 100 per cent stake in the club through intermediate holding company CovCityCo Ltd. He is a hands-on executive chairman who made his money as CEO of Yelo Enterprises, a large-scale agricultural processing and refining company.

‌



View 22 Images King helped finance Coventry's promotion (Image: Getty)

He is also the co-founder of the commodity investment firm RCMA Capital. King originally bought an 85 per cent stake from SISU Capital before buying out the remaining shares weeks later, clearing the club's debt. Coventry City Football Club Limited is the commercial entity that runs the club daily.

Crystal Palace

The Eagles' ownership structure saw them ousted from the Europa League last season and although things worked out well with them winning the Conference League, changes have been made.

Crystal Palace still operate under a multi-partner ownership model. Still, the largest investor is now Woody Johnson, co-owner of the NFL's New York Jets and heir to the Johnson & Johnson pharmaceutical and healthcare fortune.

‌



View 22 Images Johnson bought out Textor in 2025 (Image: Getty)

His stake stands at 43 per cent after he bought out John Textor's shares. It was Textor and his Eagle Football Holdings that caused the UEFA issue, as he was also the majority holder of French club Lyon at the time they qualified for the Europa League alongside Palace.

But Textor sold his significant stake to Johnson in June 2025 for £190m. American private equity investors Josh Harris and David Blitzer each hold a 10 per cent stake, whilst Steve Parish holds a 10 per cent stake. He serves as the active operating chairman. The other 27 per cent includes minority stakeholders and partners, like South African businessman Robert Franco.

Everton

The Friedkin Group owns 99.5 per cent of Everton through its subsidiary, Roundhouse Capital Holdings Limited, after buying out Farhad Moshiri's stake in December 2024. Approximately £68m was paid to Moshiri and over £250m of debt was cleared.

‌



The American sports and entertainment investment group is headed by billionaire Dan Friedkin, who amassed his fortune through automotive distribution, luxury hospitality and entertainment.

View 22 Images The Freidkins have assumed control at Hill Dickinson Stadium (Image: Getty)

Italian side AS Roma are also owned by the group and Dan is the Toffees' chairman. His son Ryan also helps oversee the club. The other small 0.5 per cent of Everton Club Company Ltd is spread out across roughly 1,500 to 2,000 small retail shareholders, fan investors and other figures.

For example, the estate of late Everton chairman Bill Kenwright holds around 1,750 shares. Local families and fans also bought single shares or small batches over the decades. Many are represented by the Everton Football Club Shareholders' Association.

‌



Fulham

Pakistani-American billionaire Shahid Khan is the 100 per cent owner of Fulham. He amassed his fortune through automotive components supplier Flex-N-Gate and also owns the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars.

View 22 Images Khan played a significant role in bringing NFL games to the UK (Image: Getty)

Khan purchased the Cottagers from long-time owner Mohamed Al-Fayed in 2013 for £150m. Whilst he supplies overall financial backing and ultimate control, his son Tony serves as vice chairman and director of football operations. K2TR Family Holdings 2, Corp is the ultimate parent company.

Hull City

The Tigers' owner made a splash this summer by taking to social media to tease fans about players he would be signing. Turkish media mogul and entrepreneur Acun Ilicali does not shy away from the spotlight.

‌



Through his firm Acun Medya, he acquired 100 per cent of Hull City in January 2022 from the Allam family for £30m, ending years of animosity. He is the chairman and sole shareholder.

View 22 Images Hull City's owner is as outspoken as they come (Image: Getty)

Under his umbrella entity, he acquired a controlling stake in the Slovenian club NK Maribor in 2024 and is also a major shareholder of Fenerbahce, serving on the club's executive board and as vice president. He owns TV8 and TV8.5, a Turkish free-to-air TV channel. Hull's ownership is controlled through a corporate chain.

Ipswich Town

The Tractor Boys' ownership structure is rather complicated. The club is operated through Ipswich Town Football Club Company Ltd, which is 99 per cent owned by parent holding company Gamechanger 20 (GC 20). The other one per cent is held by legacy fan shareholders via Ipswich Town PLC.

‌



Gamechanger 20 itself is controlled by multiple different shareholders, the majority being Portman Holdings LLC. This syndicate was created to reorganise internal shares and is controlled equally by three key investor groups, which own a combined 45 per cent of the club.

ORG Portfolio Management, led by Ed Schwartz, manages funds for another investor, the Arizona Public Safety Personnel Retirement System. They originally held a 90 per cent direct majority in 2021 before diluting their stake. Three Lions Fund, comprised of US-Turkish sports investors Brett Johnson, Berke Bakay and Mark Detmer, is also part of this group, as is Calara Vista Partners, led by Bob Gold.

View 22 Images Singer Ed Sheeran has sponsored his club's shirts in the past (Image: Getty)

Then, Bright Path Sports Partners, a US private equity firm that invested £105m into Gamechanger, owns 43 per cent of the club. They acquired their stake in March 2024. Aside from these two shareholders at 45 and 43 per cent, there are a series of other minority investors.

‌



Singer Ed Sheeran owns 1.4 per cent of his beloved club and the remaining 10.6 per cent is residual direct equity, retained individually by Johnson, Bakay and Detmer, alongside former stakeholders. To clarify, then, GC20 owns 99 per cent of Ipswich Town. Portman Holdings owns 45 per cent of GC20, Bright Path Sports Partners owns 43 per cent of GC20, and the rest is split between other minorities.

Leeds United

Leeds United are entirely owned by 49ers Enterprises. This American investment group is directly linked to the NFL's San Francisco 49ers and initially acquired a minority stake in 2018, then completed a full buyout in 2023 for £170m.

It acquired Andrea Radrizzani's remaining 56 per cent stake. The syndicate is chaired by Paraag Marathe, who is the primary executive and holds voting control, along with Jed York.

View 22 Images Marathe is the 49ers Enterprises president (Image: Getty)

‌



Energy drink company Red Bull purchased a minority equity stake in 49ers Enterprises in May 2024. As part of the deal, they became the primary front-of-shirt sponsor, but their stake is non-controlling, so they have no say in football operations and no seat on the board.

Liverpool

The Reds are primarily owned by Fenway Sports Group, a conglomerate headed by principal owner John W. Henry. FSG acquired the club in 2010 and is a 58-62 per cent owner, paying around £300m.

Henry amassed his billions in finance and commodities trading. Tom Werner is the chairman of FSG and his wealth was built as a television producer in the US.

View 22 Images Henry often attends games at Anfield (Image: Getty)

‌



The conglomerate holds key partnerships with multiple investors. NBA legend LeBron James purchased a two per cent stake in the club in 2011, and he converted that into an equity holding in FSG in 2021. RedBird Capital Partners, another private equity firm led by Gerry Cardinale, bought an 11 per cent stake in FSG in 2021.

This summer, FSG sold a 38 per cent minority stake in Liverpool to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led by Amit Bhatia that includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin. The other three to four per cent is owned by Dynasty Equity.

Manchester City

City Football Group owns 100 per cent of Manchester City. This is a multi-club network in which Newton Investment and Development LLC, owned by UAE Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, holds an 81 per cent controlling stake.

US private equity firm Silver Lake owns around 18 per cent, whilst China Media Capital holds the remaining one per cent. Ultimate financial and geopolitical control rests with Mansour, but operational leadership and day-to-day governance are exercised by Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Ferran Soriano.

‌



View 22 Images Sheikh Mansour oversaw the takeover of City in 2008 (Image: Getty)

Mansour is a member of the Al Nahyan ruling royal family of Abu Dhabi. His wealth stems from state oil and natural gas reserves and he purchased City in 2008 for approximately £210m from Thaksin Shinawatra, the former Prime Minister of Thailand.

City Football Group operates a vast global network. To name a few, they hold large stakes in New York City FC of the MLS, the A-League's Melbourne City FC, Italian side Palermo and Spanish team Girona.

Manchester United

The much-debated Glazer family, led by executive co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer, retains majority equity of Manchester United and holds around 71 per cent of shares. But United now operate under a split control structure between the Glazer family and British billionaire and entrepreneur Sir Jim Ratcliffe, founder of INEOS.

‌



View 22 Images The Glazer family have proved hugely divisive during their reign (Image: Getty)

In 2024, Ratcliffe bought a 27.7 per cent stake in the club for £1.25bn via his Trawlers Limited, a holding company incorporated on the Isle of Man. Ratcliffe soon upped this to 28.94 per cent via an additional £238m and shares were transferred to INEOS Services Limited, a subsidiary of the wider INEOS group.

United use a complex holding chain design, formed during the Glazer family's 2005 buyout. They completed the purchase for £790m. Manchester United plc, incorporated in the Cayman Islands, is the top-level parent equity and is listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

UK-based intermediate holding companies, primarily Red Football Holdings Limited and Red Football Limited, sit below. Manchester United Football Club Limited is the primary UK operational subsidiary that holds the stadium, player registrations and more.

‌



View 22 Images Ratcliffe is worth around £15bn (Image: Getty)

The club's ownership is also split into two distinct share tiers. Class B shares, which count as 10 votes per share, are non-public shares that accrue voting power. These are owned by both the Glazer family trusts and Ratcliffe. Class A shares are traded on the NYSE and count as one vote per share.

Ratcliffe's multi-billion-pound personal fortune was built almost entirely through his 67 per cent personal ownership of INEOS. CEO Omar Berrada handles footballing operations, but Joel and Avram Glazer remain co-chairmen.

Newcastle United

The Magpies are owned by a consortium led by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, the Public Investment Fund (PIF). It holds an 85 per cent majority stake. The remaining 15 per cent is owned by the British-based Reuben family via RB Sports & Media, following the departure of former minority partner Amanda Staveley in July 2024.

‌



View 22 Images Al-Rumayyan is the Magpies' chairman (Image: Getty)

Staveley's PCP Capital Partners had owned 10 per cent, but this was sold to the Reubens and the PIF. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of the PIF, serves as club chairman.

The club operates under Newcastle United Football Club Limited, which sits under ultimate parent holding entities Newcastle United Limited and NCUK Investment Limited. The consortium purchased Newcastle United in October 2021 from Mike Ashley for £305m via St James Holdings Limited.

Nottingham Forest

Nottingham Forest's owner needs no introduction. Greek shipping magnate and media tycoon Evangelos Marinakis acquired the club in May 2017 from Fawaz Al-Hasawi for £50m.

‌



View 22 Images Marinakis often ruffles feathers (Image: Getty)

Marinakis owns Forest through an intermediate holding vehicle, NF Football Investments Limited. This parent holding company holds 100 per cent of the operational entity, Nottingham Forest Football Club Limited. Marinakis is the 80 per cent owner and Greek businessman Sokratis Kominakis owns 20 per cent.

Forest's primary owner amassed his wealth via his Capital Maritime & Trading Corp. He also acquired a controlling stake in Olympiacos FC in 2010 and expanded his empire in 2023 by purchasing Rio Ave FC.

Sunderland

French-Swiss businessman Kyril Louis-Dreyfus holds a majority 64 per cent stake in the Black Cats, who are owned by Sunderland Limited. This parent holding company controls 100 per cent of the operational club entity.

‌



The Swiss-French heir to the Louis-Dreyfus Group commodities trading empire serves as chairman and majority owner. His father, Robert, was formerly the owner of Marseille and CEO of Adidas. Kyril secured an initial 41 per cent stake in 2022, and it has only increased since.

View 22 Images Louis-Dreyfus shares ownership with Sartori (Image: Getty)

The other 36 per cent of Sunderland is owned by Uruguayan billionaire, politician, and founder of Union Capital Group, Juan Sartori. He serves as a non-executive director and bought into the club in 2018.

Tottenham

Spurs are operated by Tottenham Hotspur Limited, which is split into two groups of shareholders. Around 11.7 per cent of the shares are split among almost 30,000 individual supporters, left over from before the club was privatised. ENIC Sports & Developments Holdings Limited then owns the other 88.3 per cent stake.

‌



They hold controlling voting power and equity in Spurs and paid an initial £22m in 2001 as part of a phased acquisition. Inside ENIC, the parent company is split into three distinct groups. The Lewis Family Trust is the largest owner with 72.6 per cent of ENIC. This is the discretionary trust of the Joe Lewis family and they hold the primary controlling vote.

View 22 Images Lewis received a presidential pardon in 2025 (Image: Getty)

London-born billionaire Lewis made his money through catering, trading and global investments. His family, including daughter Vivienne Lewis and son Charles Lewis, have stepped forward since he himself took a back seat in 2022, transferring his interest to the Lewis Family trust amid legal trouble regarding insider trading. He received a full presidential pardon from Donald Trump on November 13, 2025.

Ex-Spurs chairman Daniel Levy holds a 29.88 per cent stake in the club but after stepping down in June, he attempted to sell 24.99 per cent to Eight Sports Capital, an American sports investment firm. The group claims he now only holds a 4.89 per cent share but the transaction has not yet been completed. Levy no longer sits on the executive board.

Sports.title: No Liverpool players and one Man Utd star - AI picks Premier League Team of Season so far
Sports.content:
No Liverpool players and one Man Utd star - AI picks Premier League Team of Season so far

AI has picked the Premier League team of the season so far, and you might be surprised by some of the names that have named in the starting line-up

View 4 Images Mirror Sport tasked AI to come up with the Premier League Team of The Season so far. (Image: Getty Images)

It's been a blistering start to the 2026/27 Premier League campaign with Enzo Maresca's Manchester City leading the way heading into the first international break of the season. The Italian is undefeated since returning to the Etihad Stadium and City look set to rival Arsenal in the title race once again.

‌



Mikel Arteta's side lost their 100 per cent win record last time out, when they were well beaten by Brighton & Hove Albion, but the Gunners are still second in the table. Arsenal made a bright start to the season but find themselves three points behind City.

‌



The Seagulls are in third following that impressive win over the Gunners, while Brentford occupy the final spot in the top-four. The latter two clubs were in contention for European football last season and have picked up where they left off.

‌



We asked Google Gemini to construct the Premier League Team of the Season so far, and players from the aforementioned four teams are featured in the starting XI. Using underlying statistics, metrics, and media coverage from the opening five gameweeks of the 2026/27 season, it named the 11 best players so far, and you might be surprised by some of those involved.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Goalkeeper

Lukas Hornicek (Newcastle United): Despite Newcastle's mixed start, Hornicek leads the Premier League in saves (16), consistently keeping his team in matches with crucial shot-stopping.

The Czech shot stopper only signed for the Magpies in the summer transfer window in a £25.7m deal from Braga but has already had a major say in their early season results.

View 4 Images Newcastle United goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek has impressed so far this season. (Image: PA Wire)

‌



Defenders

Right-Back: Jack Hinshelwood (Brighton & Hove Albion): The England youth international is excelling in Brighton's fluid system. Hinshelwood has already contributed two goals this season while remaining incredibly solid in possession.

Centre-Back: Dan Ballard (Sunderland): The Sunderland defender has shown no sign of second season syndrome and has been a physical force at the back. He leads the league in aerial duels won (20) and is ranking near the top for total duels won (33).

Centre-Back: Lewis Dunk (Brighton & Hove Albion): Dunk is statistically the best ball-playing defender in the league so far this season. He has completed 360 passes so far and heavily dictates the tempo of Brighton's dominant possession game.

‌



Left-Back: Joško Gvardiol (Manchester City): A staple in early Team of the Season selections, Gvardiol has successfully balanced defensive solidity with significant attacking output and high ball-recovery numbers.

View 4 Images Josko Gvardiol has started the season well for Manchester City. (Image: (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images))

Midfielders

Central Midfield: Vitaly Janelt (Brentford): The Brentford midfielder currently boasts the highest average statistical rating in the league (7.71). Janelt leads all players in interceptions (16) and anchors Brentford's midfield brilliantly.

‌



Central Midfield: Pascal Groß (Brighton & Hove Albion): The creative engine of the league so far, Groß sits firmly at the top of the charts for both chances created (13) and key passes (13).

Central Midfield: Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United): Although United continues to rebuild, Fernandes is once again a standout individual, registering three goals, leading the league in total shots (16), and consistently driving the attack forward.

View 4 Images Pascal Gross has been a standout performer for Brighton & Hove Albion. (Image: (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images))

‌



Forwards

Right Winger: Bukayo Saka (Arsenal): The England international has three goals to his name and 14 fouls won. While some have questioned his recent form, the stats show Saka has been a positive outlet on the right flank, generating a massive 3.06 expected goals (xG).

Striker: Erling Haaland (Manchester City): Unsurprisingly, leading Erling Haaland leads the line. He tops the Golden Boot race with five goals, boasting the league's highest xG (3.21) and most shots on target (9).

Left Winger: Joao Pedro (Chelsea): Joao Pedro has been arguably the most complete attacker in the opening weeks, racking up three goals and three assists while winning 34 ground duels.

Sports.title: What Mikel Arteta’s rivals think about Arsenal boss as new contract 'agreed'
Sports.content:
What Mikel Arteta’s rivals think about Arsenal boss as new contract 'agreed'

Mikel Arteta is close to signing a new contract at Arsenal with the Gunners having rewarded the Spaniard for his work at the Emirates Stadium following his appointment in 2019

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta has agreed a new deal with Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has agreed a new deal with Arsenal in a move that will be welcomed by the Gunners - but not their rivals. The Spanish coach was appointed in 2019 as a replacement for Unai Emery and has done some brilliant work with the north London side.

‌



He has completely reversed the club’s fortunes over recent years to take them from mid-table to the Premier League title. Arteta has also restored Arsenal at the top of the European game, having led them to the Champions League final last term.

‌



With Arteta now set to remain with the club for the foreseeable future, his rivals will now have to continue mulling over their attempts to get the better of him.

‌



But what have they already said? Mirror Football takes a trawl through some past interviews and press conferences to find out exactly what they think of the Arsenal boss.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Xabi Alonso

Let’s start with someone who knows Arteta very well: Xabi Alonso. The two Spaniards are childhood friends and have embarked on very similar careers, with glittering playing stints in the Premier League, while they have now turned to management.

They have already locked horns this season, with the Gunners running out 2-1 winners in the Premier League earlier this month.

Speaking ahead of that game, Alonso praised his friend for his work at the Emirates and vowed that they would never think differently of each other despite now being direct rivals.

‌



He said: “No, it [their relationship] won't change. Our friendship and mutual respect won't change because of competition, because the system he's built at Arsenal is truly remarkable, and it's a long-term process.”

Andoni Iraola

Alonso is not the only close friend that Arteta has in the Premier League. Current Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola also grew up alongside the pair in the Basque region of Spain.

And he has already played quite a crucial role in his career so far, with his former side Bournemouth having held Manchester City last season to hand the Gunners the title.

‌



Iraola claimed that it was just the reward that both Arteta and Arsenal deserved after a number of near misses.

Speaking at the time, he said: “Happy for him because I think he has done an incredible job there. For a lot of seasons very consistent. Sometimes he has been so close, the reward has probably come in the right moment."

View 4 Images Arteta and Alonso are childhood friends (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Michael Carrick

Another top-flight manager who is well-acquainted with Arteta is Manchester United boss Michael Carrick. The pair faced off on a number of occasions during their playing careers and have already sparred on the touchline.

They at first clashed back in the 2021/22 season, with Carrick overseeing an interim role at United. He was successful on that occasion with a 3-2 win and repeated that result last term.

Regardless, Carrick remains a big fan of Arteta and the work he has done in north London. He said: ''I think he's done a very good job at Arsenal and you can see they're going in a certain direction and been pretty strong with that.

‌



''He was a terrific player, very technical, and that’s the way his teams plays and obviously the way he has coached them in that style shows what type of player he was.''

View 4 Images Carrick is a big fan of Arteta's work at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Unai Emery

Arteta’s longevity at the Emirates Stadium is a huge departure from his predecessor Unai Emery. The Spaniard was afforded just 18 months in north London after replacing Arsene Wenger.

‌



And that decision looks to have been for the betterment of both Arsenal and Emery - the pair having thrived apart.

The now Aston Villa coach has praised his compatriot for steering the ship back on course. He said: “The work Arteta is doing there now is brilliant and he’s doing more or less everything I was thinking needed to be done there.”

There was a brief flashpoint between the two when Emery chose not to shake Arteta’s hand after a game but that does not appear to have caused a lasting issue since then.

‌



View 4 Images Arteta and Maresca have already clashed this season (Image: Getty Images)

Enzo Maresca

One of Arteta’s main rivals this season looks to be Enzo Maresca. The Italian has replaced both his and Arteta’s former tutor Pep Guardiola at the Etihad and will be expected to put together a title charge throughout the season.

Speaking about the pair’s learnings under Guardiola, Maresca said: “Probably we [himself and Arteta] both have to be thankful because we worked besides and next to the one that I consider the best manager in the world. Probably we both have been quite lucky to work with Pep."

‌



Roberto De Zerbi

While Maresca will be one of those plotting Arteta’s downfall, the same could certainly be said of Roberto De Zerbi. The Italian is now in charge of Arsenal’s North London rivals Tottenham.

And while some fans might be wanting some hostility between the two, De Zerbi made his admiration of Arteta clear during his spell with former club Brighton.

He said: “Arteta is a great manager. He is very young and his style is clear. I enjoy watching Arsenal games… I try to learn something when I watch them. He was lucky to work with Pep Guardiola and now I think Arteta is one of the best coaches in the world.”

Sports.title: Liverpool close in on Richard Hughes successor with FSG sporting director decision close
Sports.content:
Liverpool close in on Richard Hughes successor with FSG sporting director decision close

Liverpool's majority owners, Fenway Sports Group (FSG), have been pondering who to replace Richard Hughes with following his departure as sporting director earlier this month

View 2 Images Julian Ward is expected to become Liverpool's new sporting director (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group have reportedly decided to make an internal appointment to replace Richard Hughes as Liverpool's sporting director.

‌



Hughes left his role earlier this month following a turbulent summer, choosing to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal. The former Bournemouth chief spent two years in the hot seat at Anfield, overseeing the big-money transfers of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

‌



His departure followed that of Michael Edwards, who stepped down as the chief executive officer of football of FSG in July. A busy summer also saw a consortium, which includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, take over a third of the club.

‌



FSG have scoured the market for Hughes' replacement before deciding to keep things in-house by choosing Julian Ward. The Athletic reports that Ward will switch from FSG technical director to Liverpool's sporting director, with a process overseen by FSG president Mike Gordon now nearing its conclusion.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Ward has been at the club since 2012 and has held a variety of roles at Liverpool and owners FSG. He was European scouting manager for Spain and Portugal, then loan pathways manager and then assistant sporting director.

Ward was promoted to become sporting director following the departure of Edwards in the summer of 2022, but stepped down at the end of the 2022/23 season, shocking Liverpool in the process. He returned to the fold by following Edwards to FSG in 2024, where he has been tasked with overseeing player development pathways and the academy, and is now returning to Anfield as sporting director.

During his short-lived previous spell as sporting director, Ward oversaw the signings of Luis Diaz, Darwin Nunez and Cody Gakpo, among other players. He was also behind the arrival of Alexis Mac Allister in the summer of 2023, having stayed longer than his exit date to seal the deal for the Brighton midfielder.

‌



View 2 Images Julian Ward (second left), with Michael Edwards (centre) and Richard Hughes (second right) (Image: Nikki Dyer - LFC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

It means that David Woodfine will remain as Liverpool's assistant sporting director, working underneath Ward, while Pedro Marques - who was another candidate for the role and a close colleague of Ward - will stay as FSG's director of football development.

FSG did speak to external candidates, including Brentford technical director Lee Dykes, before deciding to elevate Ward back into the hot seat. He will therefore take charge of player recruitment at Liverpool following a difficult summer.

Article continues below

Hughes' spell in charge was bookended by the £123million signing of Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while Victor Munoz, Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo all also arrived this summer. But the slow-burn nature of the summer transfer window raised plenty of eyebrows and caused some friction, with Mark Burchill and Craig McKee also leaving the club to follow Hughes to Saudi Arabia.

Andoni Iraola, who arrived following an impressive spell at Bournemouth to replace Arne Slot, was exasperated by the club's transfer business, which saw a net spend of £172m accumulated.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney makes Man Utd transfer claim on JJ Gabriel's next club decision
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney makes Man Utd transfer claim on JJ Gabriel's next club decision

There is a lot of talk over where JJ Gabriel's future could lie after he asked to leave Manchester United

View Image JJ Gabriel has told Manchester United of his desire to leave the club. (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney has claimed that a move to Spain could be on the cards for JJ Gabriel, with the youngster's exit from the club an open secret to those close to the situation. The 15-year-old has told the club that he wishes to leave.

‌



Talks have been held with Barcelona and Real Madrid over a potential move, although United could block the exit, with a tribunal then needed to sort the situation. Gabriel was expected to be part of the squad and potentially make his first-team debut for United in the Carabao Cup clash vs Brighton before the news broke.

‌



Rooney made the breakthrough as a teenager at Everton, with his son, Kai, also now playing in the United academy set-up. The former striker has suggested that a move to Spain could be the most likely option, despite the club doing everything possible to try and convince him to stay.

‌



Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest READ MORE :

Speaking on Disney+'s Stick to United, Rooney said: "I think that anyone close to it knew that was coming. In fairness to Manchester United, they've done everything, they've done absolutely everything to keep him, to keep him at the club.

"I think it's been known that there's been a desire to go and play probably in Spain, I think, I might be wrong, but this is what you've heard over the years. The club have treated him probably differently to the other players because he is such a special talent.

"I know, I recognise, I understand that because I was that player at Everton and I was getting that treatment at Everton which was you're getting a bit more, your parents get given stuff, you're getting that special treatment more than the other players are getting. Which as a club you need to do to try and keep your better players.

‌



"It's just disappointing, of course, because he is such a top player and he's a lovely kid. So you never know whether it's gone too far and whether there is a chance to stay.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"But I think everyone close to it has probably known that that was going to come".

‌



Gabriel ranks among the brightest prospects in the United youth set-up. Despite his tender age of 15, he has netted 29 times and registered four assists across 32 outings for the club's Under-18s side.

He has also bagged two goals and laid on two assists in two matches for the Under-21s.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Article continues below

Addressing the matter, United manager Michael Carrick is determined to shield the youngster from undue pressure. "He's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important that we certainly don't play anything out here," he said.

"I think the exposure and the scrutiny and everything, you've got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything. So the situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's okay is the important thing."

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho given fresh escape route after nightmare Aston Villa start
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho given fresh escape route after nightmare Aston Villa start

Former Manchester United star Alejandro Garnacho only joined Aston Villa from Chelsea in the summer but the forward could potentially be on the move once again, with clubs already eyeing him

View 2 Images Garnacho joined Aston Villa from Chelsea in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Alejandro Garnacho is reportedly being monitored by Spanish clubs after a difficult start to life with Aston Villa. The former Manchester United man only joined the Midlands side on a season-long loan deal in the summer from Chelsea.

‌



But Garnacho, 22, has been limited to just 31 minutes of action so far this season, and has not even come off the bench in any of Villa’s last three games.

‌



His switch to Villa Park will become permanent for a fee of around £43million should certain conditions be met. But that already appears unlikely.

‌



According to Mail Online, clubs in La Liga are watching Garnacho’s situation. The forward was actually born in Madrid and had a spell with Atletico Madrid’s academy before his switch to Manchester United.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Asked recently what Garnacho needs to do to earn an opportunity with the club, Villa boss Unai Emery said: “Continue working. Work, work, train, work.

“When he can have minutes to play, try to play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now. George Hemmings is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. [Ibrahim] Mbaye also responded well.

“We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs.”

‌



View 2 Images Garnacho has played just 31 minutes for Aston Villa this season (Image: Getty Images)

Having been left out of the latest Argentina squad, he will now join Villa on a mid-season training camp in Spain, where he will certainly hope to catch Emery’s eye.

Garnacho’s career has taken a sharp downturn over recent seasons. After scoring 26 goals in 144 appearances for Manchester United, he left the club in a £40m move to Premier League rivals Chelsea last summer.

Article continues below

He netted eight goals in 43 appearances for Chelsea across his debut campaign but just one of those came in the Premier League. New boss Xabi Alonso made it clear that he had little future at Stamford Bridge ahead of his move to Villa. Garnacho has just under six years remaining on his current contract at Stamford Bridge.

Villa have a just under three-week wait for their next Premier League game which is set to come against Brentford on October 10. They will then take on Fenerbahce in their first Champions League home game of the campaign.
