World.title: Saved by the Bell Star Mario Lopez Films Campaign in Costa Rica
World.content:
Mario Lopez, the actor best known as A.C. Slater on the 1990s sitcom “Saved by the Bell,” is in Costa Rica filming a campaign in the mountains of Pérez Zeledón. The actor and TV host shared the trip Tuesday in an Instagram video shot on a grassy ridge with mountains rising behind him. “Jaguars, bird-eating spiders and some serious Jurassic Park vibes. Just another day at the office,” he wrote in the caption, tagging the post #PerezZeledon.

In the video, Lopez said he was high in the mountains surrounded by jungle and that the views made the job feel less like work. He did not say what the campaign is for or who hired him, and the post does not tag a brand or production company. He also passed along what sounded like a safety briefing, saying he had been told to watch out for jaguars and for giant spiders that catch small birds in their webs. Lopez called it all part of the Costa Rica adventure and said he expected to be largely offline until Friday.

Costa Rican fans quickly filled the comments, welcoming him to Costa Rica and in several cases, to their hometown. The warnings are less far-fetched than they sound. Pérez Zeledón sits at the foot of Chirripó National Park and the Talamanca range, where jaguars still roam.

The cats are shy and mostly nocturnal, however, and attacks on people in Costa Rica are extremely rare. Most residents never see one, which is why a single camera-trap sighting still makes news, as when a jaguar reappeared on the Osa Peninsula earlier this month.

The spider is most likely the golden silk orb-weaver, a large species common in Costa Rican forests that is not considered dangerous to people. Its unusually strong webs have occasionally been documented trapping small birds. This is not Lopez’s first visit. He vacationed in Costa Rica with his family in March 2019, when immigration officials confirmed he had entered the country on March 26 and left four days later.

During that trip he posted a video from a jungle hike in which a guide taught him local expressions including “mae,” “tuanis” and “pura vida.” Pérez Zeledón, in southern San José province, is the main gateway to Cerro Chirripó, our country’s highest peak at 3,821 meters (12,536 feet) and to the rivers and cloud forests of the El General valley.

World.title: ‘Belize Is In Trouble’: Pastor Louis Wade says Government must act now, get children out of Carnival after viral video
World.content:
‘Belize Is In Trouble’: Pastor Louis Wade says Government must act now, get children out of Carnival after viral video

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Church Senator Pastor Louis Wade says the viral video showing a young boy engaged in highly sexualized dancing with three adult women at the Orange Walk Carnival demonstrates what he describes as a dangerous lack of boundaries between adult Carnival revelry and children.

Speaking with BBN on Tuesday following a strongly worded statement from the National Evangelical Association of Belize (NEAB), Wade said the churches will not remain silent on the issue and argued that authorities must establish minimum standards governing the participation and exposure of children at Carnival events.

“The church cannot remain silent, will not remain silent,” Wade said, adding that the latest incident reinforced concerns previously raised by religious groups about the direction Carnival has taken.

Wade said he also saw footage involving a young girl and an adult woman and argued that the fact such videos are recorded and publicly posted indicates that sexualized behaviour involving children is becoming normalized in some sections of society.

“Belize is in trouble if the Government does not act now to put in place minimum standards and get our children out of Carnival,” Wade said.

He argued that the Orange Walk festivities further blurred the separation between adult and junior Carnival participation, noting that children were dressed in costume designs similar to those worn by adults.

Wade also criticized what he described as the suspension or relaxed enforcement of normal standards during Carnival, questioning why conduct considered inappropriate toward a child in other settings should be treated differently because it takes place during festivities.

Despite his strong criticism, Wade stopped short of calling for Carnival itself to be cancelled, saying the churches have not reached that position and continue to support September Celebrations and cultural activities.

“We need to do better than this gutter product that we are currently displaying to the world,” Wade said.

His comments follow NEAB’s call Tuesday for police action against the three adult women seen in the viral Orange Walk video. The organization also said that if the boy’s mother recorded and posted the footage, she should face police action, and called for officers assigned to Carnival events to intervene when adults engage children in sexualized behaviour.

Police have since confirmed that inquiries will be made. During Tuesday’s press briefing, police said the Department of Human Services should also be made aware of the matter and stressed that parental consent or a parent’s unwillingness to make a complaint would not prevent authorities from acting where the welfare of a child is concerned. Police said the best interests of the child remain paramount.

Facebook also removed the video after it was posted by BBN, determining that the footage violated its rules concerning child sexual exploitation.

The controversy echoes a similar incident during the 2024 Belize City Carnival, when then-Commissioner of Police Chester Williams described sexualized dancing by an adult woman with a young boy as “tantamount to an assault of a sexual nature upon that child.”

Earlier this month, before the Orange Walk incident, the Belize Council of Churches had already called for clearer Carnival costume standards, greater modesty and particular safeguards where minors are involved, while also saying it did not seek to diminish Carnival as a cultural tradition.

World.title: Drones, BDF and community members join search for missing police officer Kenyon Barrow
World.content:
Drones, BDF and community members join search for missing police officer Kenyon Barrow

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Belize Police Department says an extensive search remains underway for Police Constable Kenyon Barrow, with police, Belize Defence Force personnel and community members now using drones to search heavily vegetated areas around his Orange Walk residence.

Barrow, 24, is attached to the Orange Walk Police Formation and was formally reported missing by a relative on September 17.

Police said Tuesday that Barrow had not reported for duty since July 30 and had been recorded as absent without leave. During that period, officers reportedly made several attempts to contact him at his residence and by telephone.

According to police, a relative was able to maintain some communication with Barrow and last spoke with him on September 8. The two reportedly arranged to meet, but Barrow did not show up. Police said their investigation indicates he was last seen leaving his residence around September 11.

Earlier public reports placed his last known recorded sighting shortly after midnight on September 12, when surveillance footage reportedly showed him leaving a residence on West San Martin Street in Trial Farm Village alone. Barrow had reportedly agreed to collect his partner from the Philip Goldson International Airport but never arrived.

Police also confirmed that the department’s welfare section had previously been in contact with Barrow, but said there had been no indication that would have caused officers to anticipate his disappearance.

Authorities stressed that there is presently no evidence to indicate that Barrow has met with foul play. Anyone with information is asked to call 911, Crime Stoppers at 922 or contact the nearest police station.

World.title: Delisha Estrada’s death ruled homicide after post-mortem reveals blunt craniofacial trauma; Michael Williams toxicology results pending
World.content:
Delisha Estrada’s death ruled homicide after post-mortem reveals blunt craniofacial trauma; Michael Williams toxicology results pending

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police say a post-mortem examination has determined that 21-year-old Delisha Estrada died from blunt craniofacial trauma and her death has now been classified as a homicide, while toxicology results remain pending in the death of her common-law partner, 31-year-old Michael Williams.

The young couple was found dead inside their Hillview-area home in Santa Elena Town on September 14 after relatives became concerned when they failed to collect their child. Their bodies were already in an advanced state of decomposition.

Police said Tuesday that Williams’ post-mortem examination listed severe pulmonary edema as his cause of death. Investigators are now awaiting toxicology results to determine whether additional factors contributed to his death.

Estrada’s examination, meanwhile, found that she died from blunt craniofacial trauma. Police said the nature of her injuries indicates they may have been inflicted by another person.

Authorities stopped short of classifying the case as a murder-suicide, stressing that the investigation remains ongoing and that no conclusions have yet been reached regarding who inflicted Estrada’s fatal injuries.

Police had previously confirmed that Estrada made several domestic violence reports before her death. Investigators also recovered items of interest from the residence.

Police say the autopsy findings have provided investigators with new information as they attempt to reconstruct what happened inside the home.

World.title: Teen stopped for pellet gun at horse race but arrested after dropping 9mm bullet; Fined $4,000 but avoids jail
World.content:
Teen stopped for pellet gun at horse race but arrested after dropping 9mm bullet; Fined $4,000 but avoids jail

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 19-year-old construction worker from Crooked Tree Village avoided immediate imprisonment on Tuesday after pleading guilty to keeping ammunition without a gun licence following a police search at a horse race in Burrell Boom.

Ismael Isac Adolphus was charged after police allegedly found him with a pellet gun and later recovered a single 9mm round during the encounter at the Castleton Horse Track on September 20.

Adolphus, who appeared unrepresented before the Chief Magistrate, pleaded guilty to keeping ammunition without a gun licence.

According to police, officers conducting searches at the horse track noticed what appeared to be a firearm tucked into Adolphus’ waistband. When questioned, he allegedly told officers that he had documentation for the weapon and led them to a brown Honda CR-V parked outside the venue.

Police say Adolphus retrieved the item from the vehicle and it was determined to be a pellet gun, which was incapable of firing live ammunition.

During the encounter, however, a bronze-coloured 9mm round reportedly fell to the ground. Police said Adolphus did not have a gun licence authorizing him to possess live ammunition.

In court, Adolphus told the Chief Magistrate that the pellet gun belonged to his uncle and that he did not know carrying it to the event would create a problem.

“I never know it was illegal,” he told the court, adding that he had no intention of harming anyone.

While possession of the pellet gun itself did not form the basis of the criminal charge, the live ammunition did.

Because Adolphus is a first-time offender, the Chief Magistrate requested the intervention of the Community Rehabilitation Office to assess whether an alternative sentence may be appropriate instead of imprisonment.

Adolphus was offered bail of $4,000 with two sureties of $2,000 each, which he was able to meet.

His bail conditions include reporting to a police station weekly, remaining free of new criminal charges and not applying for travel documents or visas while the matter remains before the court.

Adolphus is due back in court on October 5, 2026, for sentencing.

World.title: Mark Swift remanded after teens allegedly shot at on LaCroix Boulevard; gun found in drain
World.content:
Mark Swift remanded after teens allegedly shot at on LaCroix Boulevard; gun found in drain

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 28-year-old Belize City businessman was remanded to the Belize Central Prison on Tuesday after being charged in connection with an alleged shooting involving two teenage boys and the subsequent discovery of a loaded revolver in a drain.

Mark Anthony Ryan Swift, of LaCroix Boulevard, appeared unrepresented before the Chief Magistrate in Court #1, where he pleaded not guilty to keeping an unlicensed firearm, keeping ammunition without a gun licence and aggravated assault.

Due to the nature of the firearm charges, Swift was denied bail and remanded until November 13, 2026.

The charges stem from an incident shortly before 1:00 a.m. on Saturday, September 19, when police on mobile patrol reportedly encountered two boys, ages 15 and 16, running along Police Street.

According to police, the teenagers told officers that a man they identified as Swift had just fired a shot at them with a revolver. The boys accompanied police back toward LaCroix Boulevard and allegedly pointed out Swift near the corner of Police and Rootsville streets.

Police allege that when Swift was detained, he told officers that the teenagers had been harassing him and offered to show police where he had thrown the gun.

Officers subsequently searched a dried drain in the area and reportedly recovered a rusty revolver bearing the serial number “5823.” Police say the weapon contained six rounds in its chamber — five live .38 rounds and one spent casing.

The teenagers later gave statements in the presence of a Justice of the Peace.

According to their account, the 16-year-old had gone outside a Police Street residence to lock a gate when he encountered Swift allegedly armed with a .38 revolver. The 15-year-old subsequently came outside looking for his friend and allegedly heard Swift threaten to kill the 16-year-old.

The boys said they ran and that Swift pursued them before allegedly firing a shot in their direction. Neither teenager was reported injured.

Police detained Swift and later charged him with aggravated assault, keeping an unlicensed firearm and keeping ammunition without a gun licence.

The allegations against Swift have not been proven in court.

World.title: Seven-months pregnant in jail for a crack pipe: Woman remanded after old $155 fine blocks her bail
World.content:
Seven-months pregnant in jail for a crack pipe: Woman remanded after old $155 fine blocks her bail

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 35-year-old woman who is seven months pregnant was remanded to the Belize Central Prison on Tuesday after an outstanding court fine prevented her from taking up bail on a charge of possession of utensils used for smoking a controlled drug.

Leeanna Monique Samuels, a self-employed cosmetologist of Banak Street, Belize City, appeared unrepresented before a Magistrate in Court #5 after police allegedly found a silver pipe during a search on Tigris Street earlier Tuesday.

Police allege that around 10:30 a.m., officers conducting searches approached a room where Samuels was seated on a plastic chair. Police say she was holding a silver pipe in her right hand and dropped it to the floor after being informed that a search would be conducted.

The pipe, measuring about 3¼ inches, was later described by police as having been made or adapted for smoking crack cocaine or another controlled drug.

Samuels initially pleaded guilty, but when the facts were read to her, she disputed the police account. She told the court that the pipe was not found in her hand, but was beneath the chair, and that something fell when she stood up before police claimed it belonged to her.

Because her explanation amounted to a possible defence and conflicted with the prosecution’s facts, the Magistrate declined to accept the guilty plea and entered an equivocal plea of not guilty on her behalf.

Samuels was offered bail in the sum of $400 with one surety, but was required to first settle an outstanding $155 fine dating back to August 2025.

Unable to pay the old fine, a warrant was prepared for Samuels to serve the default prison term, and she was escorted to the Belize Central Prison late Tuesday evening.

Her next court appearance on the crack pipe charge is scheduled for November 30, 2026.

World.title: Police to make inquiries into Carnival video; say Human Services should intervene and parental consent would not prevent police action
World.content:
Police to make inquiries into Carnival video; say Human Services should intervene and parental consent would not prevent police action

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Belize Police Department says it will make inquiries into a viral video showing three adult women engaging in highly sexualized dancing with a young boy during the Orange Walk Carnival, stressing that a parent’s consent would not necessarily prevent authorities from intervening where the welfare of a child is concerned.

The issue was raised with police during a press briefing on Tuesday, after BBN questioned whether authorities would investigate the incident and determine whether any criminal charges could arise.

“If the circumstances are as you are relaying them to be, certainly it is a matter of concern,” police responded, adding that the Department of Human Services should also be made aware of the video.

Police said they were not previously aware of the matter but would make inquiries.

Asked whether authorities could still take action if the child’s parent consented to the behaviour or did not wish to pursue charges, police stressed that decisions involving possible abuse of a child are not left solely to a parent.

“Any abuse concerning a child, that discretion is not left to the parent to decide whether or not actions should be taken,” police said, pointing to the role of social workers and the Human Services Department.

Police noted that in other child abuse cases, a parent may not want charges pursued against an alleged offender, but Human Services can still intervene independently. The best interests of the child, police said, remain the paramount consideration.

The comments come hours after the National Evangelical Association of Belize (NEAB) called for arrests over the video. In a statement reported earlier by BBN, NEAB described the incident as an “abusive sexual situation involving a child” and called on the Government and Police Department to enforce existing laws.

NEAB said the adult women involved should face police action and went further, saying that if the boy’s mother was the person who recorded and posted the footage, she should also face arrest. The organization also called for police officers deployed at Carnival events to be instructed to intervene when adults engage children in sexualized behaviour.

The video, highlighted by BBN earlier Tuesday, was recorded during Monday’s September 21 Orange Walk Carnival Road March and shows the boy dancing closely behind three different adult female revelers at separate points as they bend and dance provocatively in front of him. The woman who originally posted the video identified the child as her son.

The scenes have drawn comparisons to a similar incident during the 2024 Belize City Carnival. At the time, then-Commissioner of Police Chester Williams described an adult woman’s sexualized dancing with a young boy as “tantamount to an assault of a sexual nature upon that child.”

Williams stressed that the fact the boy appeared to be laughing did not mean he understood what was happening to him, and police subsequently announced an investigation. Belize Carnival Association President Patrick Thompson also condemned the behaviour at the time.

Facebook has since removed the latest Orange Walk video from BBN’s page after determining that it violated the platform’s rules relating to child sexual exploitation.

Police acknowledged Tuesday that Carnival raises a broader national discussion involving culture, personal views and morality, saying the controversy invites a larger conversation about what Belizeans are prepared to accept or embrace.

However, as it relates specifically to children, police made clear that a parent’s approval or unwillingness to pursue action does not necessarily end the matter, with Human Services empowered to intervene where the best interests of a child are at stake.

World.title: Belizean Coast Guard officer makes history with Gunnery Training in India
World.content:
Belizean Coast Guard officer makes history with Gunnery Training in India

By Zoila Palma: Chief Petty Officer Windel Ogaldez has made history as the first Belizean to attend the Gunnery Instructors Foreign Course in India, representing the Belize Coast Guard alongside military personnel from 10 countries.

The course, held at INS Dronacharya, focuses on weapons systems, sensors, weapons training, small arms and the instruction of military personnel.

The Belize Coast Guard said the training will enhance Ogaldez’s professional expertise, with the knowledge and experience expected to contribute to weapons training and institutional development within the Service upon his return to Belize.

The training also marked a special moment of friendship between Belize and India as the Indian Navy joined Ogaldez in commemorating Belize’s 45th Independence Anniversary on September 21.

The Belize Coast Guard expressed appreciation to the Government of India, the Indian Navy and the leadership and instructional staff of INS Dronacharya for the training opportunity.

World.title: Chilling confession
World.content:
Murder victim 64-year-old domestic helper Hyacinth Rose Johnson, who was also called June.

FRANKFIELD, Clarendon — Police here say a 15-year-old schoolboy has been charged with murder after he confessed to using a screwdriver to fatally stab his 64-year-old neighbour then dragged her body to hide the gruesome crime.

The victim, Hyacinth Rose Johnson, a domestic helper, was killed in Union district, Grantham, north-west Clarendon in July.

“The police continued their investigation, which led them to the arrest of this young man. He was arrested on Saturday and on Monday, while being interviewed in the presence of his mother and two justices of the peace, he confessed to using a screwdriver to stab the female to death. He indicated that he was not provoked by the female, and that he doesn’t know why he [killed] her. The incident occurred at his home, which is in front of the home of the deceased,” a police source told the Jamaica Observer Tuesday.

Police dispelled rumours that Johnson, also called June, had been sexually assaulted by her killer. Police said the teen, who is a student at a prominent high school, confessed to moving the woman’s body to the back of her house.

“We have no evidence that she was sexually assaulted. Her clothing was found in a certain position; that is why persons were of the view that she was sexually molested. She was drawn by him, in a bid to hide the crime, from his premises to another premises. In the process [her underwear] were pulled down to her ankles,” the police source said.

A police report outlined that about 7:00 am on July 1 residents of Union stumbled upon Johnson’s body at the back of her house. Police said the body had stab wounds to the chest. Five days later, placard-bearing residents dressed in red and black marched through the community, protesting Johnson’s gruesome murder.

Member of Parliament for Clarendon North Western Richard Azan said Johnson was a mother of four who lived alone.

“People are outraged about it, because June was not a person who gave trouble. June went around washing and cleaning [homes] for people. She was a hard-working churchwoman. I said it at the funeral [on August 29], and I said it at a community meeting. I said we have to find this one; that was clear in my mind and we arranged community meetings and all of that with the police and everybody,” said Azan.

“I am so disappointed that a young person could be able to [allegedly] commit a crime on someone in a community who gave service to the same community by helping other persons. She could be the grandmother of the person [accused of] committing the crime,” added Azan.

World.title: NROCC to fix Catherine Hall flood woes
World.content:
Councillor Dwight Crawford with a team from the St James Municipal Corporation cleaning drains in Catherine Hall Monday.

MONTEGO BAY, St James — The agency executing the Montego Bay Perimeter Road project has rejected often-made suggestions that the ongoing work is to be blamed for flooding now plaguing the Hurricane Melissa-battered communities of West Green and Catherine Hall in St James. The National Road Operating and Construction Company (NROCC) has also promised a long-term fix for the issue, while the local authorities work on short-term solutions.

“The flooding in Catherine Hall and West Green is not related to the project,” NROCC Managing Director Stephen Edwards told the Jamaica Observer Tuesday morning.

“West Green and Catherine Hall have a history of flooding; the drains are inadequate,” he added.

His comments came a few hours after residents staged a protest to call attention to the water logged area. It was brief but caused significant disruption to traffic which was already moving at a snail’s pace.

The area has had periods of heavy rain since last week, resulting in flooding that brought back memories of last October’s Category 5 storm and fresh agony for some homeowners who have had to place furniture on blocks to keep them dry. Some residents insist that the ongoing roadwork has clogged drains which were never fully cleared after Melissa.

However while NROCC’s Edwards agrees the drains are clogged, he maintains the debris in them is unrelated to the perimeter road project and solely to debris from the storm. He pointed out that the drains being installed along the roadway, as part of the project, have been operating well so far.

“They are wide enough where a bobcat can drive through and so it can manage the water levels,” Edwards explained.

Although the two flood-prone communities do not fall directly under NROCC’s remit, he said the agency has a plan for the area.

“We are mobilised in the area, for the Montego Bay Perimeter Road Project, and we have engineers in the space; we have a contractor in the space and we’re going to take a look at it… as part of the comprehensive drainage study that we’re doing,” he promised.

The hydrological and drainage study, Edwards said, is expected to cover the wider parish in an effort to mitigate flooding challenges. However, he noted that the process would take time and requires proper preparation to ensure communities receive the best support possible.

“We’re going to do something that is going to alleviate the problem not only in the short term but the long term as well, but it needs a proper plan,” Edwards insisted.

“[Residents] are traumatised and they have been going through it; even from before Melissa that place would flood,” he added, noting that project contractors have been helping to clean drains in the two communities.

Councillor Dwight Crawford (Jamaica Labour Party, Spring Garden Division) has also been doing his part by leading a team from the St James Municipal Corporation.

“I was there on Sunday, I was in about eight inches of water but we managed to alleviate the challenges. We are employing all kinds of different avenues so we managed to alleviate the challenges in that area,” he told the Observer Tuesday.

According to Crawford, the team made significant headway in removing silt build-up from sections of the drains in Catherine Hall, allowing water that had accumulated after recent rains to run off.

However, he stressed that the flooding is not widespread.

“I know naturally when persons hear Catherine Hall and they hear floods, they think that the whole place is under water; the whole place is not under water. There are some areas where the drains are giving us some challenges. There are about three areas, two of which I think we have managed to remedy,” Crawford said.

“I know [residents] are traumatised but I wanted to show them that we are here with them, working for them to ensure that the challenges are alleviated,” he assured.

World.title: King Charles responds to Jamaica’s reparations petition; refers matter to Privy Council
World.content:
King Charles and Jamaica's Culture Minister Olivia Grange

Britain’s King Charles has referred Jamaica’s petition for reparations for chattel slavery that was filed on 7 September to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council.

Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport, Olivia Grange made the disclosure in a statement to the House of Representatives on Tuesday.

“We are awaiting directions from the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council as to the next steps to be taken in the case. We will keep the Cabinet and the Parliament updated on the developments,” she said.

Grange reminded that the filing of the petition was in keeping with the instructions of the House that “Jamaica should pursue reparations in the name of our African ancestors who endured hundreds of years of enslavement on this island, and in the name of the people of Jamaica”.

The effort is being spearheaded by the National Council for Reparations whose purpose is to research and advise the government on the pathway to reparatory justice.

Grange said the refusal of the United Kingdom to meaningfully engage on reparatory justice was what caused Jamaica to consider other options.

“We have chosen to pursue a legal pathway. A matter such as this might have been considered by the International Court of Justice. However, our advice is that Jamaica is prevented from commencing inter-state litigation against the United Kingdom before the International Court of Justice”.

Grange explained that the UK has placed specific reservations on the compulsory jurisdiction of the ICJ which prevent the Court from adjudicating on disputes between the United Kingdom and the government of any other country which is or has been a Member of the Commonwealth.

To overcome the hurdle, the reparations committee relied on the advice of the highly-regarded veteran attorney-at-law Frank Phipps. The advice was for Jamaica to petition the King using colonial law.

Grange also noted some of the criticism that followed the petition.

“We see that commentators have taken issue with the term petition, suggesting that we are going to the King on our knees. It’s simply the name of the process which is really a right to ask the King, the Head of State, to take some action on behalf of the people of Jamaica,” she said.

Grange highlighted that the ancestors who survived the Middle Passage and were taken to Jamaica endured the most horrific experience.

“Their status as human beings was denied. They were categorised as chattel, which means property that was bought, sold, and branded with hot irons to signify them as belonging to specific enslavers.

“They were abused with impunity — men, women, girls, and boys. They were raped. They were made to breed. They were forced to work for free. This went on everyday for hundreds of years. It was the gravest crime against humanity,” she remarked.

Grange said it was not enough for the leaders of countries that enslaved our ancestors to regret the suffering that slavery inflicted and to say to us let’s build a new future.

“They credit themselves with ending slavery without consideration of the successful struggle for freedom by the ancestors themselves including great heroes such as the Right Excellent Nanny of the Maroons, the Right Excellent Sam Sharpe, Tacky, Kojo, Accompong, and many others.

“Must we congratulate the arsonist for putting out the fire?”

-Lynford Simpson

World.title: ‘Not the full picture’: Gov’t rejects Opposition ‘robbery’ claims over hurricane housing costs
World.content:
Houses in Whitehouse, Westmoreland, left in ruin by Hurricane Melissa. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

The Ministry of Economic Growth and Infrastructure Development is pushing back against criticism from the Opposition over the cost associated with the installation of semi-permanent housing units for Hurricane Melissa victims in Westmoreland and St Elizabeth, arguing that the figures being cited do not reflect the full scope of the project.

Speaking at the People’s National Party annual conference on Sunday, the part’s general secretary Dr Dayton Campbell accused the Government of carrying out “robbery in plain sight” in relation to the costing of the project. Campbell, who is the Member of Parliament for Westmoreland Eastern, said a team that includes him and his councilors “put up over 40 homes in Eastern Westmoreland” and, every base he and his team erected, were done at a cost between $60,000 and $80,000.

READ: ‘Daylight robbery’

Pointing to the $1 billion value of the government contract to mount the semi-permanent houses, and the fact that the National Housing Trust had already procured the container homes, Campbell argued that it meant that the government was “going to spend $3.7 million to build a foundation to put a container house on.”

However, in a release on Tuesday, the ministry noted that while it welcomes public scrutiny of the recovery programme, “it is important that a discussion of the associated costs reflect the full scope of what is being procured and delivered, rather than characterising a comprehensive site-development, servicing and housing-installation package simply as the cost of ‘building a base’.”

It said the suggestion that the Government is spending approximately $3.7 million merely to construct a concrete “base” or “foundation” for each housing unit does not accurately reflect the scope of the contracted works.

“The intervention provides for a comprehensive package of site development, structural, plumbing, sanitation and installation works required to establish a safe and functional housing site,” the ministry said.

According to the ministry, there are three distinct units, requiring distinct construction needs. Depending on the type of unit and the specific requirements of each site, the works include site preparation and excavation; reinforced concrete foundations and footings; structural anchoring systems; entrance and exit steps; plumbing and sanitary connections; solar generator/electrical works; bathroom and kitchenette works; water-tank infrastructure, including the provision of bases for water tanks; wastewater treatment and disposal systems; preliminaries, including security arrangements for materials stored on site; and the transportation and installation of the housing unit, the ministry stated.

It said there is no flat cost for every housing unit. The cost varies according to the type of unit and the conditions and requirements of each beneficiary site.

The ministry said its costing has also been informed and corroborated by estimates obtained from the National Works Agency (NWA) and costings from the municipal corporations within some of the affected parishes.

“The costings provided by these are broadly consistent with the ministry’s assessment of the works required, providing further assurance that the costs are reflective of the scope and prevailing requirements for the works and are not arbitrary or excessive,” the release stated.

Although the housing units are classified as semi-permanent, the Government has maintained that there will be no compromise on the safety and security of residents. The objective, it said, is to provide affected households with housing that is properly founded, securely anchored, adequately serviced, technically inspected and suitable for occupation, while meeting applicable technical and resilience requirements.

Further, the ministry said the rationale for the construction of robust structural bases, is that though semi-permanent containerised solutions will be placed on them, the intention is that should the beneficiaries’ circumstances improve, they could build more permanent structures on a solid base, given that provisions for water and sewerage would be already in place.

According to the ministry, the Government’s approach to the structural base reflects a longer-term consideration of the housing needs of beneficiaries, while the immediate intervention is intended to provide a safe and secure semi-permanent housing solution for families displaced or affected by Hurricane Melissa.

“The intention, where the site and design permit are concerned, is that the investment in a properly engineered structural base and supporting infrastructure will provide a platform for future improvement,” said the ministry. “In this way as beneficiaries’ circumstances improve, expansion or upgrading of the housing accommodation can be undertaken. In the same way, provision for water, sanitation and wastewater management is therefore not simply an additional cost associated with the immediate placement of a semi-permanent unit; it represents an investment in the functionality and potential future development of the site.”

According to the ministry, this approach is particularly important given the scale of devastation caused by Hurricane Melissa. The urgency of the recovery response cannot come at the expense of safe and functional housing. The programme is therefore intended to move affected families from emergency shelter towards more secure housing solutions, with the necessary supporting infrastructure, it said.

World.title: ‘Pastor shot me twice’
World.content:
SMITH... was pastor of Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James

A witness broke down in tears on Monday while recounting the terrifying ordeal of being shot twice in the back by his late pastor, Dr Kevin Smith, who had assured him that he was immortal and could not die.

The witness, who also testified that Smith emptied two firearm magazines at members of the security forces on October 17, 2021 at Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James, received permission from Justice Leighton Pusey to remove his shirt in court to show the scars from the ordeal.

Last week, the witness told the court that Smith had another member of the congregation stab him in the back. He also used the opportunity, while he was shirtless, to point to the area of his back where he had been stabbed.

Monday was the witness’s second day on the stand in the Home Circuit Court murder trial in Kingston of Andre Ruddock, who is accused of killing 39-year-old Taneka Gardner during an alleged human sacrifice ritual at the church on October 17, 2021.

Ruddock allegedly acted on the instructions of Pastor Smith, who had asked Gardner if she believed that he could bring her back to life if her throat was cut.

Gardner’s throat was subsequently cut, allegedly by Ruddock, after she gave an answer in the affirmative to Smith’s question.

The witness had testified that after Gardner’s throat was cut, Smith further instructed Ruddock to cut her head off. It was alleged that while Ruddock was doing as he was instructed, a cow broke loose from a section of the church property and Ruddock’s attention was shifted from Gardner after Smith gave more instructions for the cow to be caught and slaughtered. A member of the church allegedly chased the cow.

The witness, Gardner, and Ruddock were members of Smith’s congregation.

The witness recalled Smith walking over to him while he was on the ground in agony and stuffing his fingers in his wounds.

“I was saying, ‘I am in pain, I am in pain.’ I remember he walked over to me. I don’t remember him speaking but I can remember him pushing his fingers in the wounds in my back. On the compound, there were a lot of individuals sitting on the boardwalk. The persons he [Smith] had called to come in, they were also sitting on the boardwalk. I looked up and I saw my mom sitting there,” the witness said.

He also testified that police and soldiers came to the boardwalk.

“One of the soldiers was kicking me in my side. He was saying to me that I was shooting at him. I told him I wasn’t doing that, and a police officer came and said to the soldier to ‘Stop, don’t you see that he was shot and cramped?’

“The soldiers started ordering the other [church] members outside, telling them to hold their heads straight. They were very hostile. An ambulance came and the police assisted them to wrap my back. They placed me on a stretcher and brought me through the side gate that was there,” the witness said, explaining that Gardner’s body was still laying on the church compound at that time.

“Taneka’s body was there. Blood was there. I was able to see. I was laying face down on the stretcher so I was able to see because the compound was not dark. When I was going through the gate, I saw Andre Ruddock on the ground. He was laying on his side. I also saw Dr Smith on the ground with his hands behind him. There was nothing blocking my view. Kevin Smith was laying face down. Security forces were all over the compound. At the gate there were police and soldiers. I was taken to the Cornwall Regional Hospital,” he told the court.

The witness said Smith was the one who shot him with a firearm he had taken from a member of the church.

“There were like three police jeeps on the outside of the premises. They were opposite the gate on the other side. At that time, a police officer was climbing on the fence [to see what was happening]. Mr Smith started to say he was Elijah and he was saying just as Elijah called down fire from heaven to consume the army, he said ‘If I be a prophet of God, I call down fire from heaven to consume these 50. He said it like three times, and he then called out for a member of the Jamaica Constabulary Force who was there [as a member of the church]. She came to him and he spoke to her and she spoke back to him,” the witness said.

By that time, Gardner was already killed, allegedly by Ruddock.

The witness, who was asked by lead prosecutor LaToya Bernard to tell the court what happened after the member of the police force spoke to Smith, explained that the pastor used the gun he had received from the member of the church to open fire at the security forces who were outside the compound of the church.

“Dr Smith started shooting at the police. At that time I stepped away and went right behind a round column that was there when Dr Smith took the gun from her. I could see him firing the gun from behind the column. He was firing the gun towards the police. I wasn’t observing everything happening on the compound. I was mainly watching him and was wondering if the police were going to shoot back,” the witness told the court.

“That was why I was behind the column. When I was looking towards where the police were I could see police bending down. I did not see them return any fire. After that happened, Dr Kevin Smith then called [the police member of the church] to bring an extra magazine [for the gun]. Dr Smith continued to fire. The police did not retaliate. Outside the premises there were members from the congregation out there along with the police. Those members on the outside weren’t running or moving or anything at all. They were just out there,” the witness testified.

He said the next thing he remembered after Smith shot at the security forces were loud explosions at the gate where the police shot and killed a member of the church who was following Smith’s instructions to attack them with a knife.

After he put his shirt back on, the witness, who had been standing during his testimony, was given an opportunity to sit and compose himself while he cried.

“Yes, Mr Kevin Smith shot me. I can remember hearing loud explosions coming from right beside me, where Mr Smith was. I fell to the ground after I felt like I got a hard punch. I remember jumping up back like I was shocked. He looked on me and said to me that, ‘You are immortal and you cannot die’. Yes, that’s what he said. I could see some police officers standing at the top of where a boardwalk was. They were on the premises by this time.

“Mr Smith then spoke to Kevaughn Plummer. I can’t recall where Andre Ruddock was at the time when Dr Smith was firing at the police. Dr Smith spoke to Kevaughn Plummer and he ran towards the police to attack them. He had a knife and he ran towards them to attack them. Upon reaching close proximity to the police, I just started seeing fire coming from the police’s gun. I could hear the loud explosions. I saw when Kevaughn Plummer’s body fell to the ground. It happened so quickly. It was just a lot of shots being fired all over the compound. By that time, because of the pain I was feeling, I was laying flat on my belly at that time on the boardwalk. I was hearing a lot of shots. At that time I turned my head and saw him [Dr Smith] sitting in the same place where he was sitting when we first came up the boardwalk. He was sitting and pointing to the sky,” the witness said.

Pastor Smith died on October 25, 2021 in a motor vehicle crash on the Linstead bypass in St Catherine while being transported to Kingston to face charges.

World.title: Motorcycle mayhem
World.content:
In this file photo Inspector Amos Thompson points to a number of motorcycles that were seized by the Westmoreland police.

WESTMORELAND is recording one of its lowest murder counts in years but police say the parish is facing another public safety threat involving motorcycles, prompting a call for tougher national measures to tackle dangerous riding.

Commanding officer for the division, Senior Superintendent Othneil Dobson said the police will continue seizing and prosecuting offenders but believes the country must change its approach to the motorcycle problem.

The call comes as Westmoreland records a 29 per cent reduction in murders between January 1 and September 12, with the number falling from 28 in 2025 to 20 this year.

But while the division works to maintain the reduction in violent crime, Dobson said motorcycle-related crashes remain a persistent road safety concern, particularly in a parish where motorcycles are widely used as a means of transportation.

Speaking during a recent episode of the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s Force4Good Podcast, Dobson said the police have been carrying out daily enforcement operations, supported by specialised teams, but dangerous riding continues to result in fatalities.

“I would not sit here and tell you that most of the persons are obeying the road traffic law. Most of the accidents are a result of careless driving, persons not having the best will or thinking about the other road users. So, we have high numbers of fatalities — but it’s not a lack of trying from the police,” he said.

Dobson reported the police have recorded some success, but the recurring nature of motorcycle crashes means enforcement must be accompanied by broader public education and changes in how Jamaica manages the issue.

“As a country, we’ll have to change some of what we’re doing with motorcycles. Most of the stations in Westmoreland are overrun with motorcycles… You seize 20 or 30 bikes and you’re driving to work the next morning and you see four or five persons riding past you with new bikes. They don’t even come back to the stations to retrieve the bikes after going through the licensing process again,” he said.

“So, as a country, we have to go from a policy perspective in terms of dealing with this bike situation. We will continue to seize, we will continue to prosecute, we will continue to educate… but the penalties just have to be higher penalties as it relates to bikes,” he argued.

World.title: Love & Harmony turns 10 with a family affair at sea
World.content:
The Love and Harmony entertainment package for 2027 will include: (clockwise from top left) Aidonia, I-Wayne, D’Yani, Kevin Downswell, Beres Hammond and Sanchez.

For a decade, Love & Harmony Cruise has been bringing Caribbean music lovers together on the high seas. Next year the celebration is getting even more personal as the popular music cruise marks its 10th anniversary.

With a special Mother’s Day voyage scheduled from May 6 to 11, 2027, the whole family will be invited to celebrate a milestone that has become as much about community as it is about music.

Reggae icon Beres Hammond will be captaining the ship once more and, as it has done for the past nine years, the Love and Harmony crew expects to deliver an unforgettable experience on the high seas.

Veteran Beres Hammond will be joined by Sanchez, D’Yani, Aidonia, Kevin Downswell, and I-Wayne for the special anniversary sail dates, with more artistes and entertainment still to be announced.

The six-day, five-night experience will be a round trip from Miami aboard the Norwegian Jewel, making stops in Montego Bay, Jamaica, and Nassau, Bahamas.

But while the 10th anniversary promises the concerts, parties, and entertainment that guests have come to expect, organisers are placing a special emphasis on family this time around.

“Ten years is an incredible milestone for Love & Harmony, but what makes this anniversary even more meaningful is that we are sailing over Mother’s Day weekend,” Director of Marketing and Public Relations Ronnie Tomlinson said.

“Love & Harmony Cruise has always felt like a family reunion at sea. We have guests who return year after year, and this time we want them to bring their mothers, children, and loved ones and celebrate together. This is more than a cruise, it is six days of Caribbean culture, music, food, laughter and memories,” he said

That family-friendly approach is reflected in the offer for the 2027 sailing, with children 12 and younger sailing for free, subject to applicable taxes and fees.

And for those who have experienced Love & Harmony before, the promise is familiar: Once the ship leaves Miami, the party does not stop simply because the sun goes down.

Live concerts, themed parties, DJ experiences, karaoke, games, comedy, poolside activities, and the Captain’s Dinner will fill the schedule, while Caribbean flavours will remain an important part of the experience.

Guests can expect a mix of Caribbean and American fare alongside Norwegian Jewel’s fine and casual dining options, with Jamaican favourites such as oxtail, ackee and saltfish, jerk chicken, and curry goat among the flavours that have helped bring the island experience aboard.

While music remains the heartbeat of Love & Harmony, laughter has increasingly become part of its soundtrack and as such comedy will play a big part in the cruise’s itinerary come May. Canadian comedian Trixx will return following his appearance on the 2026 sailing, while Jamaican-British comedian White Yardie will make his Love & Harmony debut. The comedy offering adds another layer to a voyage that has evolved beyond a traditional music cruise, giving guests something to do whether they are catching a concert, lounging poolside, or simply looking for a reason to laugh.

The anniversary celebration makes its way back to Jamaican soil when the Norwegian Jewel docks in Montego Bay on Saturday, May 8. Love & Harmony will take over Tropical Bliss Beach for a special destination experience hosted by dancehall star Aidonia, giving guests the chance to trade the ship for sand, sea, and the unmistakable energy of Montego Bay. The ship is scheduled to be in port from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, allowing Harmonisers to spend the day experiencing Jamaica before returning to the vessel and continuing the anniversary festivities.

Then, on Sunday, May 9 — Mother’s Day — the ship will remain at sea.

For organisers, the timing is intentional.

Rather than rushing from one destination to another, families will have the entire day to celebrate together, surrounded by music, food, entertainment, and the community that Love & Harmony has cultivated over the past decade.

The cruise will then head to Nassau, Bahamas, on May 10 before returning to Miami on May 11.

With additional artistes, DJs, special events and anniversary surprises still to be announced, the 2027 sailing is shaping up to be both a look back at Love & Harmony’s first decade and a celebration of the people who helped make the journey possible.

World.title: THE HUNDRED THAT WASN’T ENOUGH
World.content:
Jayden Seales of Antigua and Barbuda Falcons celebrates the dismissal of Kirk McKenzie of Jamaica Kingsmen during the Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League Final on Sunday.

JAMAICA Kingsmen Captain Rovman Powell said he was proud of his team despite an eight-wicket defeat to Antigua and Barbuda Falcons in the Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League final at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados, on Sunday.

Antigua and Barbuda Falcons needed just 16.4 overs to chase down Kingsmen 170-9 and win their first-ever Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) title, turning Maaz Sadaqat’s brutal 114 from 58 balls into a footnote.

“It’s a good feeling, to be honest. I think it’s a very hard-fought campaign for us. I’m so proud of the boys,” Powell said in a televised interview.

Batting first after losing the toss, Kingsmen were 30-2 in the fourth over before Sadaqat exploded. The left-hander hammered nine sixes and eight fours in a stunning hundred, adding 80 runs for the third wicket with Saim Ayub (29) to surge to 100-2 after 10 overs where it looked like the Kingsmen would have reached the 200-run mark.

However, the Falcons’ left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqim produced the spell of the tournament — four for 14 runs from four overs — and ripped the guts from the Kingsmen’s innings. After Ayub’s dismissal at 110-3 in the 12th over, no Kingsmen batsman made double figures.

Powell said his side fell short with the bat in the second half of their innings.

“I think after the halfway stage we felt as if we were 10 to 15 runs short,” Powell admitted.

“We knew it was a pretty good batting wicket. Credit has to be given to our batters for the first 10 overs. Maaz played fantastically for us, and the partnership he strung with Saim Ayub carried us to 100 for 2 in 10 overs. It’s disappointing that as a batting group on such a good wicket we didn’t really capitalise on that start,” he further said, hailing Ayub’s removal of Rakheem Cornwall (20) at 20-1 in the first over, and Evin Lewis’s (38) fall to Vitel Lawes at 84-2 in the eighth over.

Despite these feats, however, the chase was a demolition as

Amir Jangoo (57 not out) and Hasan Nawaz (47 not out) never looked troubled as they finished the job with 20 balls to spare.

“I think as a batting group, when we lost four wickets in the middle overs, four key batters who were supposed to put the impetus on the game in the last 10 overs, and as a bowling group, we didn’t control the powerplay as well as we wanted to,” Powell said.

But for Jamaica, a team that lost its first few games and was written off, Powell said that the final itself was redemption.

“I honestly feel it’s a proud journey for us. We have accomplished a lot of things. We set out to be in the finals, and when we came to the tournament we wanted to see if we could progress all the way. It was a slow start to the competition, as we lost our first few games, but we built a little bit of momentum with our home crowd back home in Jamaica and from there the guys started to believe that we could actually play cricket,” Powell said.”

“We went to Trinidad, which is a difficult place to play cricket, and we played a very good game down there. That confidence kept building within the team. We knew that as soon as we squeezed into the last four of the competition how dangerous our team could be, and the guys just kept chipping in. Credit has to be given to them throughout the entire competition. They listened to the leadership that myself and the head coach provided and I am actually proud of the boys,” he said.

World.title: Romania’s political deadlock risks handing power to far right, PM nominee warns
World.content:
Another failure in Bucharest would set up a divisive early election in the EU’s seventh-most-populous country, where the far right is leading the polls at a moment when populist-nationalist parties are surging in countries around Europe.

Mainstream parties in Romania — a key strategic NATO ally that has suffered some spillover from Russia’s war in Ukraine — have barely fought off the far right in a series of parliamentary and presidential elections that began in winter 2024.

PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu said on Monday that the group will not vote in favor of Mureșan’s government and would only support the formation of a government it forms part of. He has not, however, closed the door to a coalition with the far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR), which has courted confrontation with Brussels and supported pro-Russian candidates. The PSD and AUR voted together to bring down the previous government earlier this year.

Mureșan called on the EU’s center-left S&D group leadership in Brussels to prevent that from happening, arguing they “are obviously responsible for what their member parties are doing” and arguing they “will have a very significant problem of credibility, shall they continue to be silent about their Romanian members partner cooperating closely with the far right.”

“As long as the European socialists are not acting to prevent this in a very credible way from happening, we cannot exclude socialists in other countries going this way, unfortunately, as well,” he added.

Grindeanu, however, has suggested that his PSD could be convinced to enter discussions with Mureșan if he agrees to include ten policy proposals identified as core for the PSD. Among them are a new push for energy infrastructure, a defense and national security uplift, public services reform and investment in education and healthcare.

World.title: Burnham passes his first Trump test — but papers over the cracks
World.content:
That final comment will please Starmer, who welcomed Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy to Britain after Trump berated him in the Oval Office. But it also shows how far his relationship with Trump fell after his initial attempts to please the president in early 2025.

Burnham had the benefit of a fresh start, and ahead of his first meeting with Trump, British officials insisted he would take a less fawning approach than his predecessor. He could afford to do so, they said, because Trump’s presidency is almost at the midway point and there is less to lose.

Yet there were similarities to Starmer’s early days. Both leaders were on their best behavior, straining not to upset each other in public.

They each gave the other a free pass. Burnham sat expressionless as Trump talked about “fake news” media, while Trump did the same as Burnham talked about Britain’s recent sanctions on West Bank settlements.

Burnham raised the salience of immigration, an issue Trump invoked against Starmer, while Trump even praised Burnham’s “great election win.” (Burnham has not won a general election, merely a special election for the parliamentary seat of Makerfield.)

But some things were different. The splits between the two nations were closer to the surface than in Starmer’s first trip — and even in those cordial words for the cameras, the divides broke into the open.

World.title: Friedrich Merz has a Friedrich Merz problem
World.content:
Yet his combative public manner repeatedly gets in the way of the message. The irony is that the Merz I’ve seen away from the cameras can be engaging and capable of laughing at himself. His political problem is that too few voters ever see that side of him.

Criticism of Merz’s manner is no longer just about style. His personal manner is cited as one of the reasons the Christian Democrats fared so badly in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: For the first time in the party’s postwar history, they failed to clear the 5% threshold for entering a state parliament.

Aloof, confrontational and lacking in empathy — these have been frequent accusations as Merz has taken to the airwaves during the regional election season to fight his corner, sometimes making matters worse.

One encounter earlier this month was particularly damaging. In a televised roundtable, pediatrician and influencer Bea Merscher attacked his record on health spending as “inhumane.” Merz angrily told her she was “going too far,” described doctors as “beneficiaries” of the health system, and added: “You are doctors. You couldn’t get by without this health system.”

Fact checks found Merz largely right on the substance of health spending and reform — but he lost on tone. The public tends to prefer doctors to politicians in a bare-knuckle prime-time fight.

“His problem is that he argues with opponents as though they are another politician or a board member,” a person who worked with him in opposition told me, confidentially, so as not to draw the chancellor’s ire. “He doesn’t think about how it looks from the sofa in front of the TV.”

World.title: ‘Sweden is back’: Magdalena Andersson has big plans for Europe
World.content:
“We need a strong European Union in the world we live in today,” she told POLITICO. “With Russia still waging war in Ukraine, we have an unpredictable United States, and we have China trying to step forward — we really need the European Union to be strong.”

Sweden has an influential voice in European affairs, with an enviable economic record and numerous successful businesses, including tech successes Klarna and Spotify and manufacturing giants Volvo and Saab. If she is confirmed as prime minister, Andersson will be one of the few voices from the left among the EU’s 27 leaders, alongside Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen and the embattled Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

When it comes to beefing up the EU, Andersson’s priority is to overhaul its decision-making processes, especially at the sometimes quarrelsome European Council leaders’ summits. Andersson was in office at the time of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and remembers the difficult dynamic during sanctions discussions, when Hungary’s former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán threw obstacles in the way of agreements that required unanimous support.

The “number one” issue for giving the EU a strong voice is whether the bloc’s 27 leaders “can actually agree on things” when they sit “around the table,” she said. “Having a strong Europe — finding unanimity, how important that is for us to be strong — I think that’s the key.”

To that end, Andersson wants to scrap the rule granting a veto right to every EU member country on foreign policy. “I think it should be qualified majority … on foreign policy,” she said, adding that when Ukraine and other countries — such as candidates in the Western Balkans — join the EU, “there will be changes one way or another, and then I think this should be one of the issues discussed at that point in time.”

Raiding Russian assets

One area where EU leaders tried — and famously failed — to get a unanimous agreement was on whether or not to use Russia’s financial assets, lying immobilized in a Brussels depository, to help fund Ukraine’s mounting costs of defending itself. Efforts to secure a deal foundered last year on legal concerns from Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever.

World.title: Britain’s prisoner release scheme spooks EU neighbors
World.content:
The diplomat added embassies are also frustrated by the lack of coordination between departments on the issue.

“The FCDO always says talk to the Home Office,” the person said. “The Home Office says we should speak to FCDO — and the Cabinet Office says it has nothing to do with them.”

A third diplomat called it “a tricky situation,” saying European capitals are worried prisoners fresh out of “British jail can just pop to an airport in their home country, and are allowed to walk freely.”

A member of UK Border Force patrols at Heathrow Airport on July 16, 2019. | Daniel Leal/AFP via Getty Images

They said capitals would want more “information about the person being transferred,” but that the “Brits treat it as if there is nothing to confirm with us, and that it’s just a unilateral deportation.”

But prison reform campaigners point out that many of these offenders would face deportation at the end of their sentences anyway. The changes bring forward the point at which foreign prisoners become eligible for removal, as opposed to the outcome.

“It is up to the receiving country to decide if the prisoner should serve any prison time,” said Mark Day, deputy director at the Prison Reform Trust. “Some foreign nationals who are deported may not be required to serve any form of sentence. For others, the sentence served may be more punitive than the one they would have experienced in the U.K.”

World.title: Trump’s Greenland deal, explained
World.content:
Under the deal, the U.S. military will have “free access” to air, land and sea routes on and around Greenland between the two bases. Greenland is already home to the U.S. Pituffik Space Base, where about 150 American troops are stationed to operate a ballistic missile monitoring site to protect North America from long-range missile attack.

The deal also sets out how the U.S. could establish new drone warfare facilities — “unmanned military installations” — in Greenland with fast-track approval processes from the Danish and Greenlandic authorities. But Denmark and Greenland will have the final say on where such facilities should be located, or whether they are built at all.

Locking out the enemy

What’s also new are several clauses designed to stop potential rivals and adversaries taking a military or economic stake in Greenland in the future. It states that no non-NATO nation can open a base on the island or mine for critical minerals or rare earths without the agreement of the three signatories.

The HDMS Ejnar Mikkelsen, a Royal Danish Navy patrol vessel, sails in the waters of the Nuuk fjord, Greenland, on March 6, 2026. | Florent Vergnes/AFP via Getty Images

Trump has often spoken about Chinese and Russian military activities around Greenland, claiming earlier this year that, “if you take a look outside of Greenland right now, there are Russian destroyers. There are Chinese destroyers … there are Russian submarines all over the place. We’re not going to have Russia or China occupy Greenland, and that’s what they’re going to do if we don’t.”

NATO officials have quietly pushed back against those claims, with one diplomat saying “we’re not seeing any Chinese activity” around Greenland, while Russian movements in the High North haven’t changed significantly and there’s little, if any, Russian presence near Greenland.

Who pays?

In a recent social media post, Trump said “there will be no cost to the United States,” for rebuilding bases and expanding the U.S. presence in Greenland.

World.title: Could Europe’s start-ups help solve the power problems created by the AI boom?
World.content:
Europe’s push to build its own artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is intensifying a debate over whether its electricity system can keep pace.

 

Data-centre electricity consumption across the continent is projected to rise from 96 terawatt-hours (TWh) in 2024 to 236 TWh by 2035, according to UK-based energy think tank Ember.

Europe needs more data centres to expand its AI capacity, but they add further demand to already strained electricity grids. That power crunch is, in turn, making it harder to connect and build new facilities.

But some startups in Europe are pitching ways to tackle the region’s power crunch.

Euronews Next took a look at their efforts to reduce the electricity used for cooling, manage demand with batteries and put waste heat to use.

Startups rethink cooling with sensors, simulations and liquid

Servers generate a lot of heat, which must be removed to stop them from overheating.

Rather than relying on cooling equipment alone, UK startup EkkoSense places wireless sensors inside data-centre rooms to monitor temperature, airflow, power and cooling capacity.

Its software turns the readings into a three-dimensional view, helping operators identify equipment receiving too much or too little cooling.

In 2024, EkkoSense deployed its system across 20 data-centre sites operated by Virgin Media O2, one of the UK’s largest telecommunications companies.

The system cut cooling energy by an average of 15%, according to Virgin Media O2, saving more than £1 million (about €1,166,588) annually and the equivalent of 760 tonnes of carbon dioxide under location-based accounting.

While EkkoSense watches what is happening inside the room, German startup etalytics recreates the cooling system in a simulation.

Its software tests how chillers, pumps and heat exchangers would perform under different conditions. It then calculates how they could operate while using less electricity and keeping temperatures within safe limits.

Last year, Japanese technology company NTT tested etalytics’ simulation software at its data-centre facility in Bonn.

The electricity used by its chillers fell by 19.1% during the first months of a trial, with NTT expecting savings to reach as much as 25% over a full year.

Spanish startup Submer takes a different approach by changing the cooling hardware itself.

Its systems immerse servers in a non-conductive liquid that carries heat away directly, reducing the need for energy-intensive fans and air conditioning.

“The solution developed by Submer uses a new liquid cooling technique to increase energy efficiency by up to 50%, reduce carbon emissions from the use of refrigerant gases, reduce the footprint and improve the total cost of ownership (TCO) of data centres,” said Submer’s client Spanish telecommunications company Telefónica, in a blog post.

Related Hundreds protest Google data centre planned for small Austrian town

Software gives data-centre batteries a second job

Data centres use batteries to keep servers running during an outage. Some startups are now using those same batteries to help manage when a facility draws electricity from the grid.

Irish energy-technology company GridBeyond has developed software that controls when batteries charge and discharge in response to conditions on the electricity network.

The batteries can charge when electricity is abundant. When demand rises, they can supply some of the facility’s power, reducing the amount it needs to draw from the grid at that moment.

Its software has been installed at two Dublin data centres owned by Singaporean company Keppel DC REIT, providing a combined 8 MW of flexible capacity, according to GridBeyond.

Turning server heat into heating

Other startups are focusing on the heat produced by computing equipment.

UK start-up Deep Green places compact computing facilities next to organisations that need heat, such as swimming pools and district-heating networks.

Liquid warmed by the servers carries that heat into the neighbouring building’s heating system.

In a trial in southwest England, Deep Green told a local newspaper that donating heat to a swimming pool would cut its gas use by 62%, save more than £20,000 (about €23,331) a year and reduce its annual carbon emissions by 25.8 tonnes.

"By moving data centres from industrial warehouses into the hearts of communities, our ‘digital boilers’ put waste heat to good use, saving local businesses thousands of pounds on energy bills and reducing their carbon footprint,” Mark Bjornsgaard, CEO of Deep Green, told Exmouth Journal.

"Pools are just the start and around 30% of all industrial and commercial heat needs could be provided by this technology."

However, greater efficiency and flexibility cannot replace physical expansion. As AI demand grows, Europe will ultimately need more electricity generation and stronger grids.

According to the International Energy Agency, new grid infrastructure can take between five and 15 years to plan, approve and complete.

Still, the work of these startups could ease pressure on Europe’s power system while that infrastructure is being built.
