World.title: Tata turmoil shines light on India succession woes
World.content:
Mumbai – In little over a month, the chairman of India’s corporate giant Tata Group has gone from seeking another term to announcing his departure to returning to the role.

The saga around N. Chandrasekaran, who has headed the multi-billion-dollar empire for nearly a decade, has laid bare the succession challenge confronting India’s industrial behemoths.

The leadership battle at Tata Group, whose businesses span everything from Jaguar Land Rover cars to Apple iPhone assembly, has highlighted weaknesses in governance and the power struggle between boards and controlling families.

But the consequences extend far beyond shareholders, with a growing number of succession dramas shaking global confidence in India, whose economy relies heavily on corporate giants, analysts say.

The Tata fiasco came to a head last week when the board of Tata Sons, the group’s holding company, granted Chandrasekaran another five-year term.

The announcement came despite objections from the Tata Trusts, the philanthropic entities that control the conglomerate and which is chaired by family patriarch Noel Tata.

“The mutiny of the board against the controlling shareholder is possibly a first, and not the right precedent for corporate India,” independent advisory firm IiAS said in a note.

Tata is far from an isolated case: from banks to consumer goods, some of India’s biggest companies have been rocked by leadership exits and botched handovers in recent months.

“In the last 18-24 months, we’ve seen a number of CEOs being churned at the top,” Navnit Singh of executive search firm Korn Ferry told AFP.

“I do think boards may not be spending enough time looking at long-term succession. Often enough companies do not have a ‘hit by the bus’ contingent plan and are often caught off guard.”

The roots of the Tata conflict run deep.

For much of the year, Chandrasekaran’s future hung in the balance as Noel Tata raised concerns about losses at some group companies, investment spending and the possibility of listing Tata Sons.

– Leadership crisis –

The tensions intensified after the death of former patriarch Ratan Tata in 2024, leaving unresolved questions over how authority would be shared within India’s largest conglomerate.

“When Ratan was alive, he didn’t trust Noel Tata enough to make him the chairman of the Trusts,” said Shriram Subramanian of advisory firm InGovern.

“He didn’t ensure that there was a structured handover of power even when he was alive.”

A succession crisis has also rocked India’s largest private lender, HDFC Bank.

The bank’s chief executive Sashidhar Jagdishan declined another term last month, an abrupt departure that came after the shock resignation of its chairman, forcing directors into a hurried search for new leadership.

At Godrej Consumer Products, chief executive Sudhir Sitapati secured shareholder approval for a second five-year term in August only to resign days later, fuelling speculation about tensions between management and the founding Godrej family.

Experts say such episodes reveal a failure by boards to prepare for leadership transitions before they become crises.

“Independent directors are meant to ask the uncomfortable question, ‘who’s next, and are they ready?’ years before it becomes urgent,” said Tulsi Jayakumar, an economics professor specialising in family business.

“Instead, most boards wait for a health scare or a boardroom crisis to even put succession on the agenda. That’s not governance, that’s crisis management wearing a governance hat.”

– Ageing billionaires –

The Tata Group’s annual revenues are roughly equivalent to about five percent of India’s GDP, and it has become a key investor in strategic sectors including semiconductors, batteries and electronics manufacturing.

“When succession stumbles at a group the size of Tata, it isn’t a private family matter, it’s a systemic one,” Jayakumar said.

Such conglomerates sit at the centre of supply chains, employ hundreds of thousands of people and play an outsized role in shaping investor confidence, she noted.

“A prolonged succession fight signals to global capital that governance in India still runs on personality, not process,” she said.

The issue is particularly significant in a country where family-controlled businesses account for most economic activity.

India’s ageing billionaires are preparing for one of the biggest intergenerational transfers of wealth globally to their children — $382 billion according to UBS data — which implies a massive shake-up in the way many of these empires will be run.

That transition could reshape some of the country’s biggest corporate empires and test whether boards are prepared to manage increasingly complex successions.

“Succession planning is under far greater public scrutiny now,” said Amit Tandon of IiAS, noting that investors understand that “when the baton is passed to the next generation… it changes the trajectory of the company”.

“The best way to look at it is that succession planning is an art, not a science,” he added.

“And Indian businesses haven’t really cracked it yet.”

World.title: AI political ads warp reality ahead of US midterms
World.content:
Washington – A political ad depicts a US Senate hopeful remarking on God and gender while scrawling in a Bible with a crayon. But he never filmed the clip: it is yet another AI-generated video pushed by a rival ahead of the midterm elections.

AI-created ads — placing politicians in fictitious situations — have proliferated ahead of the November elections, a largely unregulated form of political communication that is increasingly being adopted despite a broader backlash against the technology.

Earlier this month, Republican Senate nominee in Texas, Ken Paxton, posted an AI-generated ad on X depicting his Democratic rival James Talarico saying: “Look, I always think of myself as a Christian who hates Christianity.”

The lifelike clip shows Talarico writing “let there be six genders” in a Bible with multicolored crayons. Overlaid text reads: “James Talarico wrong for Texas” and “wrong for America,” while a QR code seeks donations for Paxton.

Talarico condemned the ad, saying “they are lying about a candidate in this race” and that he favored a ban on deepfakes in political campaigns.

“These AI deepfake ads don’t add anything to our civic discourse,” he told NBC News. “They don’t do anything to elucidate the choice that’s in front of voters.”

The ad came a few weeks after a conservative nonprofit aligned with President Donald Trump released another AI clip depicting Talarico parodying Julie Andrews’s character in the hit classic Sound of Music, dressed in a jumper-style bodice and skirt and singing “My favorite things.”

– ‘Erodes trust’ –

The proliferation of AI ads in US federal, state and local elections comes against the backdrop of declining trust in the technology.

“The concern might be not that people believe the ads but the ads and general AI slop content risk people doubting everything,” Sarah Kreps, director of the Tech Policy Institute at Cornell University, told AFP.

“People might just dismiss real content as another deepfake, which erodes trust, causing voters to tune out rather than dig deeper for authenticity.”

The Wesleyan Media Project, which tracks election ad spending, has identified at least 164 political ads nationwide so far this year that were “generated or enhanced through the use of AI.” It estimates that the ads cost just under $80 million.

That tally of ads — sponsored by both Republicans and Democrats and splashed across airwaves and social media — was an undercount.

The group said it was difficult to definitively know whether AI tools had been used in some ads, especially as there were no federal mandates that political ads carry an AI disclaimer.

“Just the knowledge that the tech has become good enough to deceive the average viewer combined with the fact that it is being used in election communication is enough to undermine voters trust in the broader election communication ecosystem,” Ilana Beller, from the nonprofit advocacy group Public Citizen, told AFP.

– ‘Modern political cartoon’ –

However, cheap and widely available AI tools help save on the often exorbitant costs of producing ads.

“There’s no need to pay for a camera crew or hire actors to create good-looking content on a short timeline. They also open the door to creativity — no special effects editors required,” Isabel Linzer, from the nonpartisan Center for Democracy & Technology, told AFP.

In many cases, Linzer said, satirical or humorous AI ads serve as “the modern political cartoon.”

“A worthy question is whether using AI in political ads is a stunt that will boost a candidate through generating substantial free media attention,” she added.

The AI-generated ads could help candidates with goals such as fundraising and mobilizing supporters, but there is scant evidence that they influence how people vote, said Scott Babwah Brennen, director of the Center on Technology Policy at New York University.

“Much of this does seem to be effective in gaining attention, though it is unclear if that will translate into electoral success,” Babwah Brennen told AFP.

“As public sentiment grows against AI, it is possible that AI-generated negative attack ads could backfire — that is decreasing assessments of the producer of the ad.”

World.title: World Cup ‘not enough’ as Spain begin next chapter
World.content:
Madrid – Spain coach Luis de la Fuente will not allow the World Cup winners to rest on their laurels as they get back into action this week for the first time since their triumph.

La Roja may have conquered Europe in 2024 and then the world this summer, but when they face England in the Nations League on Saturday, they will be seeking to improve.

De la Fuente said in the aftermath of the World Cup final victory over Argentina in New Jersey in July, he was already looking to the future.

The 65-year-old signed a contract extension, keeping him with the team until 2032, earlier this week.

“In the heat of the moment, two or three minutes later, a player came up to me and said, ‘What do we still have to win?’ Well, the match against England on September 26th,” said De la Fuente.

“This team never stops. The World Cup isn’t enough — we have to be better. What we’ve achieved isn’t enough to win the next match.”

Spain’s next major target will be the 2028 European championships, where they have a chance to emulate the La Roja side that won Euro 2008, World Cup 2010 and Euro 2012.

De la Fuente admitted that repeating that feat would be tricky.

“In life it’s very hard to win, and many more (teams) lose than win,” he said.

“Repeating past successes in terms of titles… we’re going to try to be in a position to compete to win.

“Now we’re the team to beat. That’s an added motivation.”

– New faces –

Thomas Tuchel’s England, who lost to Spain in the Euro 2024 final, offer an immediate reminder of the level Spain will be expected to maintain as world champions.

De la Fuente picked a similar squad to his World Cup team for the upcoming Nations League games against England, Croatia twice, and the Czech Republic.

Teenage star Lamine Yamal, having returned to form with Barcelona, and captain Rodri remain the key figures, and are both in the running to win the Ballon d’Or, although there have been a few changes elsewhere.

Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez returned, after missing the World Cup with a foot injury, while Real Madrid defender Dean Huijsen has been recalled too.

Goalkeeper Joan Garcia’s injury opened the door to Inter stopper Josep Martinez, in-form Espanyol striker Roberto Fernandez could make his first appearance for La Roja and Ivan Fresneda earned a late call-up in place of hurt Tottenham defender Pedro Porro.

“How could there not be continuity with players who have won everything?” said De la Fuente. “But that doesn’t mean we won’t give a chance to those who are knocking on the door.”

Mikel Oyarzabal led the line for Spain through most of the World Cup, while Ferran Torres scored the winner in the final, but Fernandez can stake his claim after he was chosen over Real Madrid’s Carlos Espi.

That position in the team, among a few others, will be disputed during the Nations League and the build-up to Euro 2028, which is ideal for De la Fuente.

The coach’s message is clear, with Spain looking to progress despite the trophies they have already won, and strong competition can help foster the right environment for evolution.

World.title: Srijan Realty launches Orizon, an 8.3-Acre landmark redefining residential living on Kolkata’s Southern EM Bypass
World.content:
As Kolkataâs residential landscape continues to evolve, emerging micro-markets are gaining prominence as homebuyers increasingly seek a combination of connectivity, convenience and well-developed social infrastructure.

The Southern EM Bypass corridor, in particular, has witnessed a decade-long transformation from a peripheral suburb into one of the cityâs most aspirational residential addresses, supported by expanding metro and suburban rail connectivity, dual EM Bypass access, and a maturing ecosystem of schools, hospitals and retail destinations. Against this backdrop, Srijan Realty, one of Eastern Indiaâs most established residential developers, today announced the launch of Orizon, a 702-unit residential community spread across 8.3 acres off the Southern EM Bypass in Jagaddal, South Kolkata.

Project at a glance

Located on B.C. Roy Road in Jagaddal, with two access points off the Southern EM Bypass roughly 400 metres and 750 metres apart, Orizon comprises six high-rise towers ranging from 17 to 23 storeys, housing 702 three-bedroom residences sized between approximately 1,208 and 1,650 square feet. Roughly 80 percent of the 8.3-acre site â 85 percent including podium-level landscaping, has been kept open, an unusually low-density ratio for a development of this scale so close to the city.

Shahid Khudiram Metro Station is roughly

14 minutes away, with Sonarpur railway station around 15 minutes; Spencerâs, Wood Square Mall and Southwinds Galleria are all within a six-minute drive.

A life beyond the ordinary

Orizonâs design philosophy takes its name from the word âhorizon,â built around the idea that space, light and an unobstructed view are increasingly scarce commodities in a city that has grown denser over the past two decades.

Residences feature terrace-style and standing balconies intended to maximise natural light and cross-ventilation, while the projectâs golden faÃ§ade, visible from the EM Bypass â is conceived as a visual landmark along the corridor.

Connectivity meets calm

Despite its dual EM Bypass access and proximity to South Kolkataâs commercial nodes, the development has been planned to function as a self-contained green enclave, insulated from the congestion typically associated with high-density urban corridors.

Schools including BDM International and Narayana, along with healthcare providers such as Apollo Hospitalâs upcoming campus, Peerless Hospital and RN Tagore Hospital, are within a 20-minute radius.

Lifestyle infrastructure

At the centre of the development sits a roughly 33,000-square-foot clubhouse featuring an infinity-edge swimming pool, jacuzzi and dedicated kidsâ pool, alongside a 21,000-square-foot podium-level garden anchoring a sports arena with facilities for tennis, basketball, pickleball and badminton.

Indoor offerings extend to a gymnasium, yoga and meditation studio, squash court, co-working space, home theatre, library, and a dedicated senior citizensâ lounge, amenities the developer says are designed to serve every age group within a single community rather than cater narrowly to one demographic.

Inclusive, barrier-free design

A defining feature of Orizon is its barrier-free design, incorporating wheelchair access ramps, lift cabins wide enough to accommodate wheelchairs, Braille and voice-enabled lift controls, accessible toilets and designated accessible parking throughout common areas.

Srijan Realty positions this not as a regulatory minimum but as a forward-looking response to Indiaâs multigenerational households, where ageing parents, differently abled family members and young children increasingly share a single home and require equal, independent access to shared spaces.

Sustainability and future readiness

Orizon has been pre-certified for IGBC Platinum design, Indiaâs highest green building rating, with features including rainwater harvesting, solar power for common areas, low-flow water fixtures, energy-efficient LED lighting, organic waste management, and EV charging infrastructure.

Buildings certified to this standard typically deliver 20 to 30 percent energy savings and 30 to 50 percent water savings compared with conventional construction.

Leadership perspective

"Orizon reflects how we believe Kolkata wants to live today. Homebuyers are no longer choosing between space and connectivity, or between design and responsibility - they expect all of it together. Southern EM Bypass has moved past being an emerging corridor - it is now one of South Kolkata's defining growth engines, and we have been part of that story for over a decade.

World.title: Kharge backs Ladakh’s Sixth Schedule demand, seeks justice for four killed in Leh firing
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday said the party stood firmly with the people of Ladakh in their demand for meaningful constitutional safeguards, including Sixth Schedule status, to protect the Union Territoryâs land, employment opportunities, fragile environment, culture and identity.

In a post on X, Kharge said four young people were shot dead in Leh a year ago during protests demanding democratic and constitutional rights for the people of Ladakh.

"A year ago, four young people were shot in Leh during the agitation for the Democratic and Constitutional rights of the people of Ladakh. On Martyrsâ Day, we pay our solemn homage to them and stand in complete solidarity with their families," Kharge said in a post on X.

"The judicial inquiry into the tragic events of September 24 must establish the full truth, ensure accountability and deliver justice without fear or favour. The people of Ladakh have waited long enough for their legitimate aspirations to be addressed," he added.

On September 24, 2025, police in Leh opened fire during violent protests demanding statehood and constitutional safeguards for Ladakh, killing four people.





Kharge said that the Congress party "stood firmly" with their demand for meaningful Constitutional safeguards, including the Sixth Schedule, to protect Ladakh's land, employment, fragile environment, culture and identity.

Meanwhile, Ladakh authorities on Tuesday promised a new framework under Article 371 to provide constitutional safeguards tailored to the Union territoryâs specific needs.

âThe protection should cover our land, employment, culture, environment and natural resources,â he said.

Kundra said the new framework being worked out âconsidering the aspirations of Ladakhis does not exist anywhere else in the countryâ.

World.title: 'Decision unanimous': EC counters report of internal differences over SIR
World.content:
Opposition slams CEC

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying all decisions related to the exercise were taken "unanimously".The poll body clarified that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling, but these did not amount to disagreement with the final decisions taken by the Commission.The clarification came after an Indian Express report triggered a row by claiming that the two Election Commissioners had raised objections to the Commission's decisions 14 times over the past 10 months during the SIR exercise.EC sources told PTI that all decisions taken by the Election Commission, including those related to the SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as well as Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Responding to queries, officials said Sandhu and Joshi had flagged issues related to the deletion of names from electoral rolls in various states and the handling of voter data.Officials also pointed out that the law governing the Election Commission, as well as a Supreme Court judgment, provides that decisions should, as far as possible, be taken unanimously. Where unanimity is not possible, the majority view prevails.Meanwhile, opposition sharpened its attack on the Election Commission over the SIR, claiming it was meant to target electors not aligned to the BJP and its allies.Urging the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognizance of the issue, several opposition parties attacked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and accused him of becoming a puppet of those in power.In a social media post, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the poll panel of hatching a conspiracy to "wipe out democracy.""This is an extremely serious news that in the past 10 months, 2 Election Commissioners have registered their objections 14 times against the Election Commission's wrong decisions," Akhilesh said."This directly means that all Election Commissioners are not able to perform their rightful duties. If the members of an independent body do not have the freedom to carry out just actions or if there is no hearing of theirs, then these are extremely fatal and dangerous circumstances for democracy. For some people to betray democracy by becoming puppets of those in power is a grave constitutional crime. This is nothing less than a conspiracy to wipe out democracy," he added.Mamata Trinamool Congress (MTMC) also slammed CEC Kumar and said that the opposition should reintroduce the impeachment motion against Kumar in Parliament."Five months ago, more than 60 Rajya Sabha Members of Parliament... when only 50 were needed, wrote to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha moving a motion to remove the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, that was five months ago. Now today, after this big news break that two Election Commissioners objected to many of the CEC's actions, it's time to bring out the Rajya Sabha motion to impeach the CEC and save democracy," MTMC's Derek O' O'Brien said.The issue is likely to escalate further as leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been vehement in his criticism of the Election Commission and the SIR process, alleging that it has resulted in the denial of voting rights.

World.title: PM Modi likely to visit Canada in December to lock in trade deal: Canadian PM Carney
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada in December to seal the trade deal between New Delhi and Ottawa, Canadian PM Mark Carney said on Tuesday.

Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Carney said that the relationship between India and Canada is "exceptionally important" and claimed that both countries are looking to reach a trade deal by the end of the year.

"We're making good progress in our trade negotiations with India. It is an exceptionally important relationship, on many, many levels. People-to-people levels, security levels and also trade and economic," Carney said.

"He (PM Modi) will be visiting Canada around that time. I very much look forward to hosting him," he added.

This comes after Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal said that India and Canada have agreed to fast-track negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership, with the next round of talks scheduled to begin on October 5.

Goyal said he had concluded the fourth round of negotiations for the proposed trade agreement with his Canadian counterpart, minister of international trade Maninder Sidhu, in Mumbai last week.

"I have concluded the fourth round of negotiations for the Canada trade deal with my counterpart Mr Maninder Sidhu in Mumbai on Friday. Very productive discussions and both sides have resolved to fast-track negotiations, in view of which our team is now slated to go for the fifth round," he said.





"Fifth of October. So you can see that as the progress is taking shape, the speed of negotiations with Canada is also improving. Let's see, the next 90 days should be a very defining period in the Canada-India relationship," the minister said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

India and Canada have discussed a comprehensive trade pact for more than a decade. Negotiations were formally relaunched in March 2022, with the two sides also pursuing an Early Progress Trade Agreement as an interim step.

Nine negotiating rounds were held between 2022 and 2023 before the process was paused in August 2023 amid a period of strain in bilateral relations.

Trade talks between India and Canada restarted during the G20 summit in 2025 as both countries saw a thaw in diplomatic relations post the standoff with former Canadian PM Justin Trudeau who had blamed India for the killing of designated terrorist Hardeep Nijjar in Canada.

World.title: India teams up with EU, Canada & others to defend multilateralism; EAM says rules must be scrupulously followed
World.content:
India joined the EU, Canada, Australia and several other countries in co-sponsoring a declaration expressing a joint commitment to multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity, while expressing concern over escalating conflicts, trade disruption, power politics protectionism and coercion.

The declaration followed the announcement of a new initiative titled Partners for Multilateralism (P4M) on the margins of the UN General Assembly that aims to make multilateral bodies more ârepresentative, effective, legitimate and trustedâ through middle-power cooperation, amid growing fragmentation and violations of international law.

Drawing attention to geopolitical tensions, conflicts and extreme competition, foreign minister S Jaishankar said multilateralism will be best served when international law, rules, and norms are scrupulously observed.

Other declaration co-sponsors included Brazil, Barbados and Kenya, making P4M a diverse group of countries that bridges â unlike the G7 and BRICS - the gap between the West and Global South. After the co-sponsors, 16 other countries signed off on the declaration that flagged increasing use of economic interdependence as a source of leverage, disrupting trade, supply chains, investment and development finance in messages directed at both US and China.





The declaration stressed reform of multilateral institutions, including the UN, to promote fair trade, prevent conflicts and protect rule of law, while backing fair, open, resilient, predictable and inclusive economic cooperation, including more diversified and resilient global supply chains.

The declaration said that the multilateral system founded on the UN Charter remained indispensable, as it had helped provide a framework for peace, decolonisation, prosperity, and human dignity.

However, the declaration also said that it must now respond to a world that is more interconnected and complex, more contested and more multipolar.

âWe affirm the need to uphold and enforce the rules, principles and commitments that remain essential to international order, while renewing and reforming the multilateral system so that it is more effective, representative, inclusive and fit for purpose,â said the declaration, while stressing the joint commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, peaceful settlement of disputes and prohibition of the threat or use of force.

The inaugural meeting was co-hosted by European Council President Antonio Costa who said that the P4M will serve as a global network for dialogue, coalition-building and practical cooperation, helping us coordinate our response to shared challenges, with the UN at its core.

As he underlined the need for multilateralism to assert itself strongly in these times, Jaishankar also pointed to the issue of terrorism.

âThe future of peace and international security, of climate action and climate justice, of emerging technologies and development finance ,of countering terrorism and strengthening supply chain, and of ensuring disaster resilience and preparing for pandemics, all depend on a will to cooperate,â he said.

The minister also flagged the 4F crises of fuel, food, fertilizer and finance cannot be left to itself, saying where new capabilities and concerns arise, there is a very powerful case for frameworks and guardrails.

âWhere there is a threat of chokepoints dominance and disruption, de-risking and diversifying must be encouraged. And where there is a compelling cause or a powerful case, the like-minded must have the confidence to come together,â said Jaishankar, stressing the need for reformed multilateralism.

World.title: Cong accuses BJP of Assam attack, CM blames party’s ‘internal feud’
World.content:
GUWAHATI/NEW DELHI: Two Congress functionaries were injured and several vehicles damaged in Assam Monday after an alleged attack on their convoy in Samaguri where they were campaigning for the Oct 6 Nagaon assembly bypoll.

AICC secretary Manoj Chouhan and Assam Mahila Congress president Mira Borthakur were injured in the incident in Nagaon district. AICC in-charge of Assam, Bhupesh Baghel, was also part of the roadshow. Congress later filed an FIR at Nagaon and sought adequate security for Baghel.

Assam Congressâs media department chairperson Bedabrata Bora alleged âhired BJP goonsâ attacked the convoy with bottles, stones and bricks.

He said Chouhan suffered chest and abdominal injuries, while Borthakur sustained head injuries.

Around four vehicles, including those carrying LS MP Gaurav Gogoi and candidate Sibamoni Bora, were severely damaged, he said.

Baghel Tuesday blamed CM Himanta Biswa Sarma for the attack. âThe attack was nothing but a manifestation of Sarmaâs panic. They have already conceded defeat and are desperately trying to intimidate us into retreating indoors.

But he should know we are not people who can be frightened,â he said.

World.title: National film awards will now be at tourist destinations: Ashwini Vaishnaw
World.content:
NEW DELHI: On a day Ekta Nagar in Gujarat's Kevadia - where '

' holds centrestage - became the space for at the 72nd National Film Awards, information and broadcasting minister

on Tuesday said govt plans to take these awards to some of the best tourism destinations across states in the future.

He urged all states to send in their proposals of best tourist destinations, and prepare and execute 360 degree development plans in those areas. "The proposal of whichever state is selected, the next national film awards will be held at that tourist destination," he said.

Reflecting on PM Narendra Modi's vision when G20 summit was organised in India in 2023, Vaishnaw said that at that time too programmes related to the summit were held across different states. World.title: ED searches office of senior Punjab official over building scam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a crackdown on a nexus of senior officials of Punjab govt and builders relating to Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (Gmada), ED Tuesday searched multiple premises in Delhi, Ludhiana, Panchkula, Mohali and Chandigarh, including the office of Gmada and that of IAS officer and principal secretary (housing and urban development) Vikas Garg.

It is probing senior officials of Punjab govt and several builders and developers in connection with alleged corruption in Gmada and for the award of projects to builders through auction, waiver of external development charges, interest charges, etc.

Searches were conducted on 26 premises ârelated to Tirupati Infraprojects Pvt Ltd and its promoters, directors and associated persons, besides othersâ. The other builders under probe include Remigate Buildestates (India) Pvt Ltd, MB Infrabuild Pvt Ltd, Mera Baba Reality Associates Pvt Ltd and Mera Baba Infrastructure Pvt Ltd.

âSimultaneously, searches are being conducted at the offices of Gmada and of the department of housing and urban development, Punjab, to gather evidence from the accused entities,â sources said. âTirupati Infraprojects is also an accused in CBI and ED cases, being allegedly involved in a bank fraud to the tune of Rs 290 crore concerning a project, Radisson Blu hotel, at Paschim Vihar, New Delhi.â

ED has estimated suspected undue gain to the firms and the loss to the exchequer at more than Rs 100 crore. ED is also searching a consultancy firm, Tila Consultants & Contractors, which deals with various consultancy works of Gmada and is suspected to have acted as an intermediary in the scam.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE | Mirabai Chanu wins silver in women’s 48kg weightlifting
World.content:
Jay Meena created history by securing India’s first-ever soft tennis medal at the Asian Games, winning bronze after losing to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka in the men’s singles semifinals on Wednesday (September 23, 2026). The 26-year-old, competing at his third Asian Games, staged a spirited fightback after falling three games behind but could not sustain the momentum, going down 2-4 in a 45-minute clash.

Star Indian weightlifter Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women’s 49kg event with a total lift of 198kg, including 87kg in the snatch and 111kg in the clean and jerk, securing India’s first Asian Games weightlifting medal since Karnam Malleswari’s bronze in 1998, while double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker finished fifth in the women’s 10m air pistol final with 181.1 after qualifying third with 579 and will next compete in the 25m pistol event, where she is the defending champion.

Also Read | Asian Games 2026: Indian men shuttlers assured of a medal; women crash out

Earlier, the Indian women’s team produced a dominant performance against a Sri Lankan side that looked under pressure from the outset. Smriti Mandhana led the charge with a superb 79 as India posted a formidable 216/3.

Also Read: Asian Games 2026: Women’s cricket team clinches India’s first gold in style

India’s bowlers then took centre stage, delivering a clinical performance to skittle Sri Lanka for just 69. Led by Deepti Sharma, who finished with an economy rate of 1.50, the bowling attack kept Sri Lanka in check throughout as India romped to a 147-run victory.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 India’s medallists: Full list of winners
World.content:
The 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games are underway in Japan. With eleven medals, India is currently placed in 11th spot in the medal tally which is topped by China.

Jay Meena secured India’s first-ever soft tennis medal at the Asian Games, fetching a bronze after losing to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka in the men’s singles semifinals. Star Indian weightlifter Mirabai Chanu completed her medal collection, winning a silver medal in the women’s 49kg event in the Asian Games.

The Indian Women’s Cricket Team clinched a historic victory at the Karogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi. Facing off against Sri Lanka in a high-stakes final, the Women in Blue triumphed to secure India’s very first gold medal of the tournament.

Meanwhile, shooters have led the charge for India, garnering five medals. The women’s skeet team, comprising Raiza Dhillon, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal, won a bronze with a combined score of 331 here on September 23, 2026.

Experienced rifle shooter Elavenil Valarivan played a starring role in the country’s double-silver haul in the women’s 10m air rifle competition. Elavenil, one of India’s most accomplished rifle shooters, helped the country secure silver in the team event along with Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod. She then went on to add an individual silver.

For the men’s side, teenager Himanshu Dhillon produced a superb performance to win silver, while former world champion Rudrankksh Patil clinched bronze as India secured two individual podium finishes in the men’s 10m air rifle event. The two then teamed up with Parth Mane to win another silver in the team event, finishing just behind China.

After an impressive start in shooting, India also managed to script history in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA), with Suchika Tariyal winning the nation’s first-ever bronze medal for MMA at the Asian Games.

A contingent of 501 Indian athletes, comprising 267 men and 234 women, is competing across 36 disciplines in the 2026 edition. Apart from shooting, athletics and archery too are expected to add to the medal tally. India is also defending both the men’s and women’s titles in cricket and kabaddi.

Here’s the full list of Team India’s medal winners at Aichi-Nagoya 2026.
